non-clinical-cs-0.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-0.displayText: Implementation of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines (on-site training, facilitation by a local opinion leader [obstetrician-gynaecologist], supervision) plus audits of indications for cesarean delivery and provision of feedback to healthcare professionals are recommended to reduce overall cesarean sections. (Recommended, High-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-1.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-1.sourceText: Healthcare professionals education by a local opinion leader obstetrician-gynaecologist to promote implementation of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines is recommended to reduce repeat cesarean sections.
non-clinical-cs-1.displayText: Healthcare professionals' education by a local opinion leader [obstetrician-gynaecologist] to promote implementation of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines is recommended to reduce repeat cesarean sections. (Recommended, High-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-2.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-2.sourceText: Implementation of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines combined with structured, mandatory second opinion for cesarean section indication is recommended to reduce cesarean births only with targeted monitoring and evaluation in settings with an on-site senior clinician able to provide mandatory second opinion for cesarean section indication. (Context-specific recommendation, moderate-certainty evidence).
non-clinical-cs-2.displayText: Implementation of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines combined with structured, mandatory second opinion for cesarean section indication is recommended to reduce cesarean births only with targeted monitoring and evaluation in settings with an on-site senior clinician able to provide mandatory second opinion for cesarean section indication. (Context-specific recommendation, moderate-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-3.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-3.sourceText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, peer review plus mandatory second opinion are recommended only in the context of rigorous research.
non-clinical-cs-3.displayText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, peer review plus mandatory second opinion are recommended only in the context of rigorous research. (Context-specific recommendation, very low-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-4.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-4.sourceText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, audit and feedback plus financial incentive for health-care professionals or health-care organizations are recommended only in the context of rigorous research.
non-clinical-cs-4.displayText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, audit and feedback plus financial incentive for health-care professionals or health-care organizations are recommended only in the context of rigorous research. (Context-specific recommendation, very low-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-5.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-5.sourceText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, audit and feedback using Robson classification is recommended only in the context of rigorous research.
non-clinical-cs-5.displayText: For the sole purpose of reducing cesarean sections, audit and feedback using Robson classification is recommended only in the context of rigorous research. (Context-specific recommendation, very low-certainty evidence).

non-clinical-cs-6.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-6.sourceText: The number of women who deliver by Cesarean section has increased steadily in Egypt over the last three decades, from 4.6% in 1992 (1) to 51.8% in 2014 (2) .
non-clinical-cs-6.displayText: The number of women who deliver by Cesarean section has increased steadily in Egypt over the last three decades, from 4.6% in 1992 to 51.8% in 2014.

non-clinical-cs-7.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-7.sourceText: Cesarean birth is associated with short- and long-term risks that can extend many years beyond the current delivery and affect the health of the woman, the child, and future pregnancies.
non-clinical-cs-7.displayText: Cesarean birth is associated with short- and long-term risks that can extend many years beyond the current delivery and affect the health of the woman, the child, and future pregnancies.

non-clinical-cs-8.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-8.sourceText: Cesarean section increases the likelihood of requiring a blood transfusion, the risks of anesthesia complications, organ injury, infection, thromboembolic disease, and neonatal respiratory distress, among other short-term complications.
non-clinical-cs-8.displayText: Cesarean section increases the likelihood of requiring a blood transfusion, the risks of anesthesia complications, organ injury, infection, thromboembolic disease, and neonatal respiratory distress, among other short-term complications.

non-clinical-cs-9.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-9.displayText: Cesarean section has been associated in the long term with an increased risk of asthma and obesity in children, and complications in subsequent pregnancies, such as uterine rupture, placenta accreta, placenta previa, hysterectomy, and intra-abdominal adhesions.

non-clinical-cs-10.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-10.sourceText: High rates of cesarean section are associated with substantial health-care costs (3) .
non-clinical-cs-10.displayText: High rates of cesarean section are associated with substantial health-care costs.

non-clinical-cs-11.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-11.displayText: The international health-care community has considered the ideal rate for cesarean section to be between 10% and 15%.

non-clinical-cs-12.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-12.displayText: WHO concluded that, at population level, cesarean section rates higher than 10% were not associated with reductions in rates of maternal and newborn mortality.

non-clinical-cs-13.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-13.displayText: Every effort should be made to provide cesarean sections to women in need, rather than striving to achieve a specific rate.

non-clinical-cs-14.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-14.sourceText: The primary audience for this guideline includes health-care professionals namely obstetricians, midwives, nurses, and general medical practitioners, as well as managers of maternal and child health programs and public health policymakers in Egypt.
non-clinical-cs-14.displayText: The primary audience for this guideline includes health-care professionals namely obstetricians, midwives, nurses, and general medical practitioners, as well as managers of maternal and child health programs and public health policymakers in Egypt.

non-clinical-cs-15.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-15.displayText: The guideline uses the GRADE-Adolopment methodology adapted from existing WHO guidelines.

non-clinical-cs-16.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-16.displayText: Non-clinical interventions refer to those interventions applied independently of a clinical encounter between a particular provider and patient in the context of patient care.

non-clinical-cs-17.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-17.displayText: For women requesting a cesarean section without medical indication, explore the reasons for maternal request, offer discussion and psychological support. (Strong)

non-clinical-cs-18.bookTitle: Non-Clinical Interventions to reduce overall cesarean sections
non-clinical-cs-18.displayText: Hospital quality improvement programme and clinical audit committees review cesarean section indications and maternal outcomes using Robson classification. (Strong)

robson-classification-0.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-0.sourceText: Be aware of the cesarean section rate and its burden on health system.
robson-classification-0.displayText: Be aware of the cesarean section rate and its burden on health system.

robson-classification-1.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-1.sourceText: Help you to recognize the absolute indications of cesarean section.
robson-classification-1.displayText: Help you to recognize the absolute indications of cesarean section.

robson-classification-2.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-2.sourceText: Help you in assessing and validating the relative indications of cesarean section.
robson-classification-2.displayText: Help you in assessing and validating the relative indications of cesarean section.

robson-classification-3.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-3.sourceText: Helps you to understand and implement the Robson Classification and build the Report Table using your own data
robson-classification-3.displayText: Understand and implement the Robson Classification and build the Report Table using your own data.

robson-classification-4.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-4.sourceText: Identify the complications of cesarean section.
robson-classification-4.displayText: Identify the complications of cesarean section.

robson-classification-5.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-5.chapterTitle: How to classify women in Robson classification?
robson-classification-5.sourceText: 1 ( the current situation is single pregnancy )
robson-classification-5.displayText: The Robson Classification (10-group classification) presents a standard approach to implement and interpret the classification of cesarean sections.

robson-classification-6.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-6.chapterTitle: How to classify women in Robson classification?
robson-classification-6.sourceText: 1 ( the current situation is single pregnancy )
robson-classification-6.displayText: The Robson Classification (10-group classification) categorizes all pregnant women into 10 mutually exclusive groups based on obstetric characteristics.

robson-classification-7.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-7.sourceText: Each Robson group should be analyzed for its relative size and cesarean section rate to identify areas for intervention.
robson-classification-7.displayText: Each Robson group should be analyzed for its relative size and cesarean section rate to identify areas for intervention.

robson-classification-8.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-8.sourceText: Monitoring of cesarean section rate can be achieved through implementing the Robson classification system.
robson-classification-8.displayText: Monitoring of cesarean section rate can be achieved through implementing the Robson classification system.

robson-classification-9.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-9.sourceText: Regular audit using Robson classification should be mandatory in all maternity units in Egypt.
robson-classification-9.displayText: Regular audit using Robson classification should be mandatory in all maternity units in Egypt.

robson-classification-10.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-10.chapterTitle: What are the variables of Robson Classification?
robson-classification-10.sourceText: Singleton ( even if dead more than 22 weeks of gestation )
robson-classification-10.displayText: Fetal growth restriction in singleton or twin pregnancy requires careful classification and monitoring under Robson guidelines. (Strong)

robson-classification-11.bookTitle: Rationalizing the use of caesarean section in Egypt through implementing 10 group Classification system
robson-classification-11.sourceText: Parity, previous CS, onset of labor, gestational age, number of fetuses, lie and presentation of the fetus are the essential variables for Robson classification. (Strong)
robson-classification-11.displayText: Parity, previous CS, onset of labor, gestational age, number of fetuses, lie and presentation of the fetus are the essential variables for Robson classification. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-0.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-0.sourceText: A urinary beta-human chorionic gonadotrophin ( -hCG) test should be performed in all women of reproductive age presenting to a maternity or adult general hospital/unit with abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, gastrointestinal symptoms, dizziness, or collapse
ectopic-pregnancy-0.displayText: A urinary beta-human chorionic gonadotrophin (β-hCG) test should be performed in all women of reproductive age presenting to a maternity or adult general hospital/unit with abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, gastrointestinal symptoms, dizziness, or collapse. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-1.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-1.sourceText: A thorough gynaecological, obstetric, medical, and surgical history should be taken to assess for risk factors for ectopic pregnancy; however, half of women with an ectopic pregnancy will have no known risk factors. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-1.displayText: A thorough gynaecological, obstetric, medical, and surgical history should be taken to assess for risk factors for ectopic pregnancy; however, half of women with an ectopic pregnancy will have no known risk factors. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-2.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-2.sourceText: A physical examination, including measurement of vital signs, should be performed to assess haemodynamic stability in women presenting with the above symptoms
ectopic-pregnancy-2.displayText: A physical examination, including measurement of vital signs, should be performed to assess haemodynamic stability in women presenting with the above symptoms. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-3.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-3.sourceText: There should be prompt escalation of care if there are any red flag symptoms on triage assessment or abnormal vital signs in the presence of a positive urinary HCG
ectopic-pregnancy-3.displayText: There should be prompt escalation of care if there are any red flag symptoms on triage assessment or abnormal vital signs in the presence of a positive urinary HCG. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-4.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-4.sourceText: Offer women who attend an early pregnancy unit a transvaginal ultrasound scan to identify the location of the pregnancy and whether there is a fetal pole and heartbeat. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-4.displayText: Offer women who attend an early pregnancy unit a transvaginal ultrasound scan to identify the location of the pregnancy and whether there is a fetal pole and heartbeat. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-5.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-5.sourceText: Do not use serum HCG measurements to determine the location of the pregnancy
ectopic-pregnancy-5.displayText: Do not use serum HCG measurements to determine the location of the pregnancy. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-6.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-6.sourceText: Use serum HCG measurements only for assessing trophoblastic proliferation to help to determine subsequent management
ectopic-pregnancy-6.displayText: Use serum HCG measurements only for assessing trophoblastic proliferation to help to determine subsequent management. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-7.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-7.sourceText: Take 2 serum HCG measurements as near as possible to 48 hours apart (but no earlier) to determine subsequent management of a pregnancy of unknown location. Take further measurements only after review by a senior healthcare professional
ectopic-pregnancy-7.displayText: Take 2 serum HCG measurements as near as possible to 48 hours apart (but no earlier) to determine subsequent management of a pregnancy of unknown location. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-8.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-8.sourceText: For a woman with an increase in serum HCG levels greater than 63% after 48 hours:
ectopic-pregnancy-8.displayText: For a woman with an increase in serum HCG levels greater than 63% after 48 hours, inform her that she is likely to have a developing intrauterine pregnancy and offer a transvaginal ultrasound scan. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-9.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-9.sourceText: For a woman with a decrease in serum HCG levels greater than 50% after 48 hours, inform her that the pregnancy is unlikely to continue and ask her to take a urine pregnancy test 14 days after the second serum HCG test. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-9.displayText: For a woman with a decrease in serum HCG levels greater than 50% after 48 hours, inform her that the pregnancy is unlikely to continue and ask her to take a urine pregnancy test 14 days after the second serum HCG test. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-10.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-10.sourceText: Pregnancy of unknown location is a transient state in the diagnostic process, leading to a final diagnosis of viable or nonviable intrauterine pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, or persistent pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-10.displayText: Pregnancy of unknown location is a transient state in the diagnostic process, leading to a final diagnosis of viable or nonviable intrauterine pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, or persistent pregnancy of unknown location. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-11.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-11.sourceText: Offer expectant management as an option to women who:
ectopic-pregnancy-11.displayText: Offer expectant management as an option to women who are clinically stable and pain-free and have a tubal ectopic pregnancy measuring <35 mm with no visible heartbeat on transvaginal ultrasound scan and serum hCG levels of ≤1000 IU/L and are able to return for follow-up. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-12.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-12.sourceText: Offer systemic methotrexate to women who have no significant pain and have an unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy with an adnexal mass smaller than 35 mm with no visible heartbeat and have a serum hCG level less than 1,500 IU/litre and do not have an intrauterine pregnancy (as confirmed on an ultrasound scan) and are able to return for follow-up
ectopic-pregnancy-12.displayText: Offer systemic methotrexate to women who have no significant pain and have an unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy with an adnexal mass smaller than 35 mm with no visible heartbeat and have a serum hCG level less than 1,500 IU/litre. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-13.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-13.sourceText: It is recommended that women treated with methotrexate wait at least 3 months before trying to conceive again
ectopic-pregnancy-13.displayText: It is recommended that women treated with methotrexate wait at least 3 months before trying to conceive again. (GPS)

ectopic-pregnancy-14.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-14.sourceText: Offer surgery as a first-line treatment to women who are unable to return for follow-up after methotrexate treatment or who have significant pain, an adnexal mass of 35 mm or larger, a fetal heartbeat visible on ultrasound, or a serum hCG level of 5,000 IU/litre or more. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-14.displayText: Offer surgery as a first-line treatment to women who are unable to return for follow-up after methotrexate treatment or who have significant pain, an adnexal mass of 35 mm or larger, a fetal heartbeat visible on ultrasound, or a serum hCG level of 5,000 IU/litre or more. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-15.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-15.sourceText: Offer the choice of either methotrexate or surgical management to women with an ectopic pregnancy who have a serum hCG level of at least 1,500 IU/litre and less than 5,000 IU/litre, who are able to return for follow-up and who meet all of the following criteria:
ectopic-pregnancy-15.displayText: Offer the choice of either methotrexate or surgical management to women with an ectopic pregnancy who have a serum hCG level of at least 1,500 IU/litre and less than 5,000 IU/litre. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-16.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-16.sourceText: When surgical treatment is indicated for women with an ectopic pregnancy, it should be performed laparoscopically whenever possible, taking into account the condition of the woman and the complexity of the surgical procedure.
ectopic-pregnancy-16.displayText: When surgical treatment is indicated for women with an ectopic pregnancy, it should be performed laparoscopically whenever possible. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-17.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-17.sourceText: Offer a salpingectomy to women undergoing surgery for an ectopic pregnancy unless they have other risk factors for infertility
ectopic-pregnancy-17.displayText: Offer a salpingectomy to women undergoing surgery for an ectopic pregnancy unless they have other risk factors for infertility. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-18.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-18.sourceText: Consider salpingotomy as an alternative to salpingectomy for women with risk factors for infertility such as contralateral tube damage
ectopic-pregnancy-18.displayText: Consider salpingotomy as an alternative to salpingectomy for women with risk factors for infertility such as contralateral tube damage. (Conditional)

ectopic-pregnancy-19.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-19.sourceText: Inform women having a salpingotomy that up to 1 in 5 women may need further treatment, which may include methotrexate and/or a salpingectomy. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-19.displayText: Inform women having a salpingotomy that up to 1 in 5 women may need further treatment, which may include methotrexate and/or a salpingectomy. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-20.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-20.sourceText: We recommend against expectant management of cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy.
ectopic-pregnancy-20.displayText: We recommend against expectant management of cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-21.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-21.sourceText: We recommend that systemic methotrexate alone not be used to treat cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy.
ectopic-pregnancy-21.displayText: We recommend that systemic methotrexate alone not be used to treat cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-22.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-22.sourceText: In patients who choose continuation of a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy, we recommend repeated cesarean delivery between 34 0/7 and 35 6/7 weeks of gestation. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-22.displayText: In patients who choose continuation of a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy, we recommend repeated cesarean delivery between 34 0/7 and 35 6/7 weeks of gestation. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-23.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-23.sourceText: Offer anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis at a dose of 250 IU (50 micrograms) to all rhesus-negative women who have a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage.
ectopic-pregnancy-23.displayText: Offer anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis at a dose of 250 IU (50 micrograms) to all rhesus-negative women who have a surgical procedure to manage an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-24.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-24.displayText: Do not offer anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis to women who receive solely medical management for an ectopic pregnancy or have a pregnancy of unknown location. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-25.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-25.sourceText: An early pregnancy ultrasound scan at 6 weeks gestation should be performed in any subsequent pregnancy due to the increased risk of ectopic pregnancy recurrence.
ectopic-pregnancy-25.displayText: An early pregnancy ultrasound scan at 6 weeks' gestation should be performed in any subsequent pregnancy due to the increased risk of ectopic pregnancy recurrence. (GPS)

ectopic-pregnancy-26.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-26.sourceText: Management of Interstitial and cornual pregnancy
ectopic-pregnancy-26.displayText: Diagnosis and management of interstitial and cornual pregnancy: implantation in the uterine cornu requires specialized surgical or medical intervention. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-27.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-27.sourceText: When carrying out a transabdominal or transvaginal ultrasound scan during early pregnancy, scan the uterus and adnexa to check for heterotopic pregnancy. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-27.displayText: When carrying out a transabdominal or transvaginal ultrasound scan during early pregnancy, scan the uterus and adnexa to check for heterotopic pregnancy. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-28.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-28.sourceText: Interstitial pregnancy: Implantation in the interstitial tubal part of the Fallopian tube passing through the uterine muscle requires timely diagnosis and surgical management. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-28.displayText: Interstitial pregnancy: Implantation in the interstitial tubal part of the Fallopian tube passing through the uterine muscle requires timely diagnosis and surgical management. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-29.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-29.sourceText: Women who conceive via IVF or other assisted reproductive technologies are at higher risk for ectopic and heterotopic pregnancy and require early ultrasound assessment. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-29.displayText: Women who conceive via IVF or other assisted reproductive technologies are at higher risk for ectopic and heterotopic pregnancy and require early ultrasound assessment. (Strong)

ectopic-pregnancy-30.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy & pregnancy of unknown location
ectopic-pregnancy-30.sourceText: Pregnancy of unknown location (PUL): Take 2 serum HCG measurements 48 hours apart to determine subsequent management; place more importance on clinical symptoms than on serum HCG alone. (Strong)
ectopic-pregnancy-30.displayText: Pregnancy of unknown location (PUL): Take 2 serum HCG measurements 48 hours apart to determine subsequent management; place more importance on clinical symptoms than on serum HCG alone. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-0.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-0.sourceText: Diagnose Hypertension in pregnancy when systolic blood pressure is 140mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure is 90mmHg, based on the average of at least 2 measurements, taken at least 15 minutes apart, using the same arm. (Strong recommendation/High level of evidence). 8,9,12
hypertension-pregnancy-0.displayText: Diagnose Hypertension in pregnancy when systolic blood pressure is ≥140mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure is ≥90mmHg, based on the average of at least 2 measurements, taken at least 15 minutes apart, using the same arm. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-1.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-1.sourceText: Severe hypertension (sBP 160 and/or dBP 110 mmHg), can be confirmed within a short interval (minutes) to facilitate timely antihypertensive therapy
hypertension-pregnancy-1.displayText: Severe hypertension (sBP ≥ 160 and/or dBP ≥ 110 mmHg) can be confirmed within a short interval (minutes) to facilitate timely antihypertensive therapy. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-2.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-2.sourceText: Gestational hypertension is hypertension that develops for the first time at 20 weeks, without evidence of preeclampsia
hypertension-pregnancy-2.displayText: Gestational hypertension is hypertension that develops for the first time at > 20 weeks, without evidence of preeclampsia. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-3.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-3.sourceText: Women with gestational hypertension should undergo testing for preeclampsia to rule it out.
hypertension-pregnancy-3.displayText: Women with gestational hypertension should undergo testing for preeclampsia to rule it out. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-4.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-4.sourceText: Diagnose preeclampsia in women with new onset hypertension after 20 weeks and new-onset proteinuria or one/more adverse conditions (defined as a maternal end organ complication or evidence of uteroplacental dysfunction)
hypertension-pregnancy-4.displayText: Diagnose preeclampsia in women with new onset hypertension after 20 weeks and new-onset proteinuria or one/more adverse conditions (defined as a maternal end organ complication or evidence of uteroplacental dysfunction). (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-5.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-5.sourceText: Preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension is diagnosed by the development of 1 or more characteristics of preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension. (Strong)
hypertension-pregnancy-5.displayText: Preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension is diagnosed by the development of 1 or more characteristics of preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-6.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-6.sourceText: Risk factors for developing preeclampsia should be included in the antenatal assessment of all pregnant women. (GPS)
hypertension-pregnancy-6.displayText: Risk factors for developing preeclampsia should be included in the antenatal assessment of all pregnant women. (GPS)

hypertension-pregnancy-7.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-7.sourceText: All pregnant women should be screened for their risk of developing preeclampsia early in the pregnancy.
hypertension-pregnancy-7.displayText: All pregnant women should be screened for their risk of developing preeclampsia early in the pregnancy. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-8.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-8.sourceText: Screen for proteinuria with urinary dipstick at first visit and at each subsequent visit
hypertension-pregnancy-8.displayText: Screen for proteinuria with urinary dipstick at first visit and at each subsequent visit. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-9.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-9.sourceText: To reduce the risk of developing preeclampsia, pregnant women with one high risk factor or two or more moderate risk factors for developing preeclampsia should receive low dose aspirin (100 mg -150 mg daily) beginning at 12 weeks gestation and till delivery.
hypertension-pregnancy-9.displayText: To reduce the risk of developing preeclampsia, pregnant women with one high risk factor or two or more moderate risk factors for developing preeclampsia should receive low dose aspirin (100 mg -150 mg daily) beginning at 12 weeks gestation and till delivery. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-10.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-10.sourceText: The use of supplemental calcium is strongly recommended in pregnant women with low dietary calcium intake ( 1g/day) for the prevention of preeclampsia, preterm birth, and gestational hypertension
hypertension-pregnancy-10.displayText: The use of supplemental calcium is strongly recommended in pregnant women with low dietary calcium intake (<1g/day) for the prevention of preeclampsia, preterm birth, and gestational hypertension. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-11.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-11.sourceText: Calcium supplementation at doses of 1.5 2.0 g elemental calcium/day is recommended from the first antenatal visit till delivery, to reduce the risk of developing preeclampsia
hypertension-pregnancy-11.displayText: Calcium supplementation at doses of 1.5-2.0 g elemental calcium/day is recommended from the first antenatal visit till delivery, to reduce the risk of developing preeclampsia. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-12.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-12.sourceText: Pregnant women with hypertension or with risk factors for developing preeclampsia should be educated about the symptoms and signs that require immediate attention and referral to health care facilities.
hypertension-pregnancy-12.displayText: Pregnant women with hypertension or with risk factors for developing preeclampsia should be educated about the symptoms and signs that require immediate attention and referral to health care facilities. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-13.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-13.sourceText: Dietary salt restriction, for prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended given the lack of evidence of benefit
hypertension-pregnancy-13.displayText: Dietary salt restriction, for prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended given the lack of evidence of benefit. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-14.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-14.sourceText: The use of oral omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids supplementation for the prevention of preeclampsia is not recommended until more data are available. (Conditional)
hypertension-pregnancy-14.displayText: The use of oral omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids supplementation for the prevention of preeclampsia is not recommended until more data are available. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-15.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-15.sourceText: The use of oral vitamin C and E supplementation, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended until more data are available
hypertension-pregnancy-15.displayText: The use of oral vitamin C and E supplementation, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended until more data are available. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-16.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-16.sourceText: The use of statins, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended until more data are available
hypertension-pregnancy-16.displayText: The use of statins, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia, is not recommended until more data are available. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-17.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-17.sourceText: The use of metformin, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia is not recommended until more data are available
hypertension-pregnancy-17.displayText: The use of metformin, specifically for the prevention of preeclampsia is not recommended until more data are available. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-18.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-18.sourceText: Ambulatory outpatient management at home is an option only for women with mild to moderate gestational hypertension and requires frequent fetal and maternal evaluation
hypertension-pregnancy-18.displayText: Ambulatory outpatient management at home is an option only for women with mild to moderate gestational hypertension and requires frequent fetal and maternal evaluation. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-19.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-19.sourceText: Hospitalization is appropriate for Women with gestational hypertension in whom adherence to frequent monitoring is a concern and for patients diagnosed with preeclampsia
hypertension-pregnancy-19.displayText: Hospitalization is appropriate for women with gestational hypertension in whom adherence to frequent monitoring is a concern and for patients diagnosed with preeclampsia. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-20.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-20.sourceText: Non-severe hypertension should be treated with the first-line agents oral methyldopa, labetalol, or nifedipine
hypertension-pregnancy-20.displayText: Non-severe hypertension should be treated with the first-line agents oral methyldopa, labetalol, or nifedipine. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-21.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-21.sourceText: Severe hypertension in pregnancy (i.e., sBP 160 mmHg or dbp 110 mmHg) requires urgent antihypertensive therapy, in a monitored setting
hypertension-pregnancy-21.displayText: Severe hypertension in pregnancy (i.e., sBP ≥ 160 mmHg or dBP ≥ 110 mmHg) requires urgent antihypertensive therapy, in a monitored setting. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-22.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-22.sourceText: Severe hypertension should be treated with the first-line agents oral nifedipine, oral labetalol, IV labetalol, or IV hydralazine
hypertension-pregnancy-22.displayText: Severe hypertension should be treated with the first-line agents oral nifedipine, oral labetalol, IV labetalol, or IV hydralazine. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-23.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-23.sourceText: The target BP for antihypertensive therapy should be a dBP of 85 mmHg, regardless of sBP
hypertension-pregnancy-23.displayText: The target BP for antihypertensive therapy should be a dBP of 85 mmHg, regardless of sBP. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-24.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-24.sourceText: Use of corticosteroid (either betamethasone or dexamethasone) is recommended in women with preeclampsia who are at risk of birth at 34 weeks gestation
hypertension-pregnancy-24.displayText: Use of corticosteroid (either betamethasone or dexamethasone) is recommended in women with preeclampsia who are at risk of birth at < 34 weeks' gestation. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-25.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-25.sourceText: The use of magnesium sulphate for fetal neuroprotection in women with preeclampsia at risk of preterm birth at 30 weeks gestation is strongly recommended
hypertension-pregnancy-25.displayText: The use of magnesium sulphate for fetal neuroprotection in women with preeclampsia at risk of preterm birth at < 30 weeks' gestation is strongly recommended. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-26.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-26.sourceText: Women with mild to moderate gestational hypertension or preeclampsia without severe features should have expectant management up to 37 0/7 weeks of gestation. (Conditional)
hypertension-pregnancy-26.displayText: Women with mild to moderate gestational hypertension or preeclampsia without severe features should have expectant management up to 37 0/7 weeks of gestation. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-27.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-27.sourceText: Initiate birth at 37 weeks gestation, in women with preeclampsia
hypertension-pregnancy-27.displayText: Initiate birth at ≥ 37 weeks gestation in women with preeclampsia. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-28.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-28.sourceText: Prophylactic magnesium sulphate with an intravenous loading dose of 4g followed by maintenance at 1g/hr for 24 hours is strongly recommended in women at risk of eclampsia or recurrent eclampsia. (Conditional)
hypertension-pregnancy-28.displayText: Prophylactic magnesium sulphate with an intravenous loading dose of 4g followed by maintenance at 1g/hr for 24 hours is strongly recommended in women at risk of eclampsia or recurrent eclampsia. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-29.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-29.sourceText: Women with eclampsia should receive magnesium sulphate to prevent recurrent seizures
hypertension-pregnancy-29.displayText: Women with eclampsia should receive magnesium sulphate to prevent recurrent seizures. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-30.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-30.sourceText: For women with severe preeclampsia with features of HELLP expectant management is harmful. Plan birth as soon as feasible
hypertension-pregnancy-30.displayText: For women with severe preeclampsia with features of HELLP expectant management is harmful. Plan birth as soon as feasible. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-31.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-31.sourceText: Platelet transfusion should be considered if a woman's platelet count is <20 ×10^9/L before vaginal delivery or <50 ×10^9/L before cesarean delivery, or at any time if there is excessive active bleeding. (Conditional)
hypertension-pregnancy-31.displayText: Platelet transfusion should be considered if a woman's platelet count is <20 ×10^9/L before vaginal delivery or <50 ×10^9/L before cesarean delivery, or at any time if there is excessive active bleeding. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-32.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-32.sourceText: Vaginal delivery is the preferred modality, unless urgent delivery is necessary for maternal stabilization or for fetal indications. The delivery options should be discussed by a multidisciplinary team and consider the safest mode of delivery to the mother, how fast she is expected to deliver, what are the resources of blood products and other supportive mechanisms available, and can she sustain a surgery
hypertension-pregnancy-32.displayText: Vaginal delivery is the preferred modality, unless urgent delivery is necessary for maternal stabilization or for fetal indications. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-33.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-33.sourceText: For women with any hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, vaginal delivery should be considered unless a cesarean delivery is required for obstetrical indications. (Strong)
hypertension-pregnancy-33.displayText: For women with any hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, vaginal delivery should be considered unless a cesarean delivery is required for obstetrical indications. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-34.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-34.sourceText: Offer expectant management for women with Chronic hypertension who are 37 weeks and, whose blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg with or without antihypertensive treatment, unless there are other medical indications62
hypertension-pregnancy-34.displayText: Offer expectant management for women with chronic hypertension who are <37 weeks and whose blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg with or without antihypertensive treatment, unless there are other medical indications. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-35.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-35.sourceText: Offer antihypertensive treatment to pregnant women who have chronic hypertension and who are not already on treatment if they have sustained systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or higher or sustained diastolic blood pressure of 90 mmHg or higher
hypertension-pregnancy-35.displayText: Offer antihypertensive treatment to pregnant women who have chronic hypertension and who are not already on treatment if they have sustained systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or higher or sustained diastolic blood pressure of 90 mmHg or higher. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-36.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-36.sourceText: Offer pregnant women with chronic hypertension aspirin 150 mg once daily from 12 weeks
hypertension-pregnancy-36.displayText: Offer pregnant women with chronic hypertension aspirin 150 mg once daily from 12 weeks. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-37.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-37.sourceText: Do not offer planned early birth (before 37 weeks) to women with chronic hypertension whose blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg, unless there are other medical indications. (Strong)
hypertension-pregnancy-37.displayText: Do not offer planned early birth (before 37 weeks) to women with chronic hypertension whose blood pressure is lower than 160/110 mmHg, unless there are other medical indications. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-38.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-38.sourceText: Do not routinely limit the duration of the second stage of labour in women with controlled hypertension
hypertension-pregnancy-38.displayText: Do not routinely limit the duration of the second stage of labour in women with controlled hypertension. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-39.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-39.sourceText: As women with preeclampsia are at increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage, the third stage of labour should be actively managed
hypertension-pregnancy-39.displayText: As women with preeclampsia are at increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage, the third stage of labour should be actively managed. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-40.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-40.sourceText: Ergometrine should not be administered to women with any hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, particularly preeclampsia or gestational hypertension alternative oxytocic drugs should be considered
hypertension-pregnancy-40.displayText: Ergometrine should not be administered to women with any hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, particularly preeclampsia or gestational hypertension; alternative oxytocic drugs should be considered. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-41.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy

hypertension-pregnancy-42.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-42.sourceText: At 3 months postpartum, all women should be reviewed to ensure that BP, urinalysis, and any laboratory abnormalities have normalised. If proteinuria or hypertension persist, then appropriate referral for further investigations should be initiated
hypertension-pregnancy-42.displayText: At 3 months postpartum, all women should be reviewed to ensure that BP, urinalysis, and any laboratory abnormalities have normalised. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-43.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-43.sourceText: Following hypertensive pregnancy, particularly pre-eclampsia, counselling should be provided about the heightened health risks for the mother (particularly cardiovascular) and the offspring
hypertension-pregnancy-43.displayText: Following hypertensive pregnancy, particularly pre-eclampsia, counselling should be provided about the heightened health risks for the mother (particularly cardiovascular) and the offspring. (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-44.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-44.sourceText: The use of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) alone (without aspirin) in women without a history of thrombophilia or APLS can be considered if a contraindication to aspirin exists. (Conditional)
hypertension-pregnancy-44.displayText: The use of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) alone (without aspirin) in women without a history of thrombophilia or APLS can be considered if a contraindication to aspirin exists. (Conditional)

hypertension-pregnancy-45.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-45.sourceText: GDG recommends to nationally adopt a color-triage system for acute obstetric emergencies (Modified Early obstetric warning score -MEOWS) . (GPS)
hypertension-pregnancy-45.displayText: GDG recommends to nationally adopt a color-triage system for acute obstetric emergencies (Modified Early obstetric warning score - MEOWS). (Strong)

hypertension-pregnancy-46.bookTitle: Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension in Pregnancy
hypertension-pregnancy-46.sourceText: - Offer postnatal counselling regarding the pregnancy and birth experience including formal postnatal review to discuss the events of the pregnancy if required.
hypertension-pregnancy-46.displayText: Offer postnatal counselling regarding the pregnancy and birth experience including formal postnatal review to discuss the events of the pregnancy. (Strong)

pas-0.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-0.sourceText: The major risk factors for placenta accreta spectrum are history of accreta in a previous pregnancy, previous caesarean delivery and other uterine surgery, including repeated endometrial curettage. This risk rises as the number of prior caesarean sections increases. (Strong)
pas-0.displayText: The major risk factors for placenta accreta spectrum are history of accreta in a previous pregnancy, previous caesarean delivery and other uterine surgery, including repeated endometrial curettage. This risk rises as the number of prior caesarean sections increases. (Strong)

pas-1.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-1.sourceText: Women requesting elective caesarean delivery for non-medical indications should be informed of the risk of placenta accreta spectrum and its consequences for subsequent pregnancies. (GPS)
pas-1.displayText: Women requesting elective caesarean delivery for non-medical indications should be informed of the risk of placenta accreta spectrum and its consequences for subsequent pregnancies. (GPS)

pas-2.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-2.sourceText: Antenatal diagnosis of placenta accreta spectrum is crucial in planning its management and has been shown to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality. (Strong)
pas-2.displayText: Antenatal diagnosis of placenta accreta spectrum is crucial in planning its management and has been shown to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality. (Strong)

pas-3.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-3.sourceText: Previous caesarean delivery and the presence of an anterior low-lying placenta or placenta praevia should alert the antenatal care team of the higher risk of placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)
pas-3.displayText: Previous caesarean delivery and the presence of an anterior low-lying placenta or placenta praevia should alert the antenatal care team of the higher risk of placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)

pas-4.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-4.sourceText: Ultrasound imaging is highly accurate when performed by a skilled operator with experience in diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)
pas-4.displayText: Ultrasound imaging is highly accurate when performed by a skilled operator with experience in diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)

pas-5.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-5.sourceText: Refer women with any ultrasound features suggestive of placenta accreta spectrum to a specialist unit with imaging expertise. (Strong)
pas-5.displayText: Refer women with any ultrasound features suggestive of placenta accreta spectrum to a specialist unit with imaging expertise. (Strong)

pas-6.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-6.sourceText: Women with a history of previous caesarean section seen to have an anterior low-lying placenta or placenta praevia at the routine fetal anomaly scan should be specifically screened for placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)
pas-6.displayText: Women with a history of previous caesarean section seen to have an anterior low-lying placenta or placenta praevia at the routine fetal anomaly scan should be specifically screened for placenta accreta spectrum. (Strong)

pas-7.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-7.sourceText: Patients with previous one or more cesarean section and diagnosed as cesarean scar pregnancy at 5-6 weeks of gestation are at high risk of developing placenta accreta. They should be counseled and referred to a tertiary hospital for termination of pregnancy. (Strong)
pas-7.displayText: Patients with previous one or more cesarean section and diagnosed as cesarean scar pregnancy at 5-6 weeks of gestation are at high risk of developing placenta accreta. They should be counseled and referred to a tertiary hospital for termination of pregnancy. (Strong)

pas-8.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-8.sourceText: Clinicians should be aware that the diagnostic value of MRI and ultrasound imaging in detecting placenta accreta spectrum is similar when performed by experts. (Strong)
pas-8.displayText: Clinicians should be aware that the diagnostic value of MRI and ultrasound imaging in detecting placenta accreta spectrum is similar when performed by experts. (Strong)

pas-9.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-9.sourceText: MRI may be used to complement ultrasound imaging to assess the depth of invasion and lateral extension of myometrial invasion, especially with posterior placentation. (GPS)
pas-9.displayText: MRI may be used to complement ultrasound imaging to assess the depth of invasion and lateral extension of myometrial invasion, especially with posterior placentation. (GPS)

pas-10.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-10.sourceText: Women diagnosed with placenta accreta spectrum should be cared for by a multidisciplinary team in a specialist centre with expertise in diagnosing and managing invasive placentation. (GPS)
pas-10.displayText: Women diagnosed with placenta accreta spectrum should be cared for by a multidisciplinary team in a specialist centre with expertise in diagnosing and managing invasive placentation. (GPS)

pas-11.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-11.sourceText: Delivery for women diagnosed with placenta accreta spectrum should take place in a specialist centre with logistic support for immediate access to blood products, adult intensive care unit and neonatal intensive care unit by a multidisciplinary team with expertise in complex pelvic surgery. (Strong)
pas-11.displayText: Delivery for women diagnosed with placenta accreta spectrum should take place in a specialist centre with logistic support for immediate access to blood products, adult intensive care unit and neonatal intensive care unit by a multidisciplinary team with expertise in complex pelvic surgery. (Strong)

pas-12.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-12.sourceText: In the absence of risk factors for preterm delivery in women with placenta accreta spectrum, planned delivery at 35+0 to 36+6 weeks of gestation provides the best balance between fetal maturity and the risk of unscheduled delivery. (GPS)
pas-12.displayText: In the absence of risk factors for preterm delivery in women with placenta accreta spectrum, planned delivery at 35+0 to 36+6 weeks of gestation provides the best balance between fetal maturity and the risk of unscheduled delivery. (GPS)

pas-13.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-13.sourceText: Any woman giving consent for caesarean section should understand the specific risks of placenta accreta spectrum in terms of massive obstetric hemorrhage, increased risk of lower urinary tract damage, the need for blood transfusion and the risk of hysterectomy. (Strong)
pas-13.displayText: Any woman giving consent for caesarean section should understand the specific risks of placenta accreta spectrum in terms of massive obstetric hemorrhage, increased risk of lower urinary tract damage, the need for blood transfusion and the risk of hysterectomy. (Strong)

pas-14.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-14.sourceText: The elective delivery of women with placenta accreta spectrum should be managed by a multidisciplinary team, which should include senior anesthetists, obstetricians and gynecologists with appropriate experience. (Strong)
pas-14.displayText: The elective delivery of women with placenta accreta spectrum should be managed by a multidisciplinary team, which should include senior anesthetists, obstetricians and gynecologists with appropriate experience. (Strong)

pas-15.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-15.sourceText: Intravenous tranexamic acid should be administered at the commencement of surgery because it reduces intraoperative blood loss. (Strong)
pas-15.displayText: Intravenous tranexamic acid should be administered at the commencement of surgery because it reduces intraoperative blood loss. (Strong)

pas-16.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-16.sourceText: Caesarean section hysterectomy with the placenta left in situ is preferable to attempting to separate it from the uterine wall. (Strong)
pas-16.displayText: Caesarean section hysterectomy with the placenta left in situ is preferable to attempting to separate it from the uterine wall. (Strong)

pas-17.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-17.sourceText: When the extent of the placenta accreta is limited in depth and surface area, uterus preserving surgery may be appropriate, including partial myometrial resection. (Conditional)
pas-17.displayText: When the extent of the placenta accreta is limited in depth and surface area, uterus preserving surgery may be appropriate, including partial myometrial resection. (Conditional)

pas-18.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-18.sourceText: There is limited evidence to support uterus preserving surgery in placenta percreta and women should be informed of the high risk of peripartum and secondary complications, including the need for secondary hysterectomy. (GPS)
pas-18.displayText: There is limited evidence to support uterus preserving surgery in placenta percreta and women should be informed of the high risk of peripartum and secondary complications, including the need for secondary hysterectomy. (GPS)

pas-19.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-19.sourceText: In case of unsuspected placenta accreta spectrum diagnosed after the birth of the baby, the placenta should be left in situ and an emergency hysterectomy performed. (GPS)
pas-19.displayText: In case of unsuspected placenta accreta spectrum diagnosed after the birth of the baby, the placenta should be left in situ and an emergency hysterectomy performed. (GPS)

pas-20.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-20.sourceText: Additional possible interventions in the case of massive haemorrhage should also be discussed, including cell salvage and interventional radiology where available. (Conditional)
pas-20.displayText: Additional possible interventions in the case of massive haemorrhage should also be discussed, including cell salvage and interventional radiology where available. (Conditional)

pas-21.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-21.sourceText: Multidisciplinary planning for placenta accreta spectrum surgery includes discussing interventional radiology and cell salvage where available. (Conditional)
pas-21.displayText: Multidisciplinary planning for placenta accreta spectrum surgery includes discussing interventional radiology and cell salvage where available. (Conditional)

pas-22.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-22.sourceText: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) includes placenta increta, where chorionic villi invade into the myometrium, requiring specialized multidisciplinary surgical management. (Strong)
pas-22.displayText: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) includes placenta increta, where chorionic villi invade into the myometrium, requiring specialized multidisciplinary surgical management. (Strong)

pas-23.bookTitle: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS): Diagnosis and Management
pas-23.sourceText: There are currently insufficient data to recommend the routine use of ureteric stents in placenta accreta spectrum. The use of stents may have a role when the urinary bladder is invaded by placental tissue. (GPS)
pas-23.displayText: There are currently insufficient data to recommend the routine use of ureteric stents in placenta accreta spectrum. The use of stents may have a role when the urinary bladder is invaded by placental tissue. (GPS)

endometriosis-0.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-0.displayText: Clinicians should consider the diagnosis of endometriosis in individuals presenting with the following cyclical and non-cyclical signs and symptoms: dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia, dysuria, dyschezia, painful rectal bleeding or haematuria, shoulder tip pain, catamenial pneumothorax, cyclical cough/haemoptysis/chest pain, cyclical scar swelling and pain, fatigue, and infertility. (GPS)

endometriosis-1.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-1.displayText: Offer an abdominal and pelvic examination to people with suspected endometriosis to identify abdominal masses and pelvic signs, such as reduced organ mobility and enlargement, tender nodularity in the posterior vaginal fornix, and visible vaginal endometriotic lesions. (GPS)

endometriosis-2.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-2.sourceText: Women with suspected endometriosis should have further diagnostic steps, including imaging, even if the clinical examination is normal. (Strong)
endometriosis-2.displayText: Women with suspected endometriosis should have further diagnostic steps, including imaging, even if the clinical examination is normal. (Strong)

endometriosis-3.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-3.sourceText: 10, 20, 21 1.3.2 Clinicians are recommended to use imaging (US or MRI) in the diagnostic work-up for endometriosis, but they need to be aware that a negative finding does not exclude endometriosis, particularly superficial peritoneal disease (low level of evidence, strong recommendation) .
endometriosis-3.displayText: Clinicians are recommended to use imaging (US or MRI) in the diagnostic work-up for endometriosis, but they need to be aware that a negative finding does not exclude endometriosis, particularly superficial peritoneal disease. (Strong)

endometriosis-4.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-4.sourceText: 10, 20, 22-26 1.3.3 Offer a transvaginal ultrasound scan to all women with suspected endometriosis, even if pelvic or abdominal examination is normal, to identify ovarian endometriomas and deep endometriosis (very low level of evidence, conditional recommendation) .
endometriosis-4.displayText: Offer a transvaginal ultrasound scan to all women with suspected endometriosis, even if pelvic or abdominal examination is normal, to identify ovarian endometriomas and deep endometriosis. (Conditional)

endometriosis-5.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-5.sourceText: 13 1.3.5 Do not use pelvic MRI as the primary investigation to diagnose endometriosis in people with symptoms or signs suggestive of endometriosis (very low level of evidence, conditional recommendation).
endometriosis-5.displayText: Do not use pelvic MRI as the primary investigation to diagnose endometriosis in people with symptoms or signs suggestive of endometriosis. (Conditional)

endometriosis-6.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-6.sourceText: 1.4 Laparoscopy: surgical diagnosis: 1.4.1 In patients with negative imaging results, or where empirical treatment (hormonal contraceptives or progestogens) was unsuccessful, consider offering laparoscopy for the diagnosis and treatment of suspected endometriosis (GPS) .
endometriosis-6.displayText: In patients with negative imaging results, or where empirical treatment (hormonal contraceptives or progestogens) was unsuccessful, consider offering laparoscopy for the diagnosis and treatment of suspected endometriosis. (GPS)

endometriosis-7.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-7.sourceText: 1.5 Biomarkers: 1.5.1 Do not use serum CA125 to diagnose endometriosis ( moderate level of evidence, Strong recommedation) . 10, 11, 13
endometriosis-7.displayText: Do not use serum CA125 to diagnose endometriosis. (Strong)

endometriosis-8.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-8.sourceText: Treatment of endometriosis associated pain 2.1 Pain control in endometriosis 2.1.1 For women with pain associated with endometriosis-, consider a short trial (for example, 3 months) of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) alone or in combination with paracetamol, if not contraindicated.
endometriosis-8.displayText: For women with pain associated with endometriosis, consider a short trial (for example, 3 months) of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) alone or in combination with paracetamol, if not contraindicated. (GPS)

endometriosis-9.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-9.sourceText: 11 2.2 Hormonal treatment for endometriosis 2.2.1 It is recommended to offer women hormone treatment (combined hormonal contraceptives, progestogens, GnRH agonists or GnRH antagonists) as one of the options to reduce endometriosis-associated pain (moderate level of evidence, strong recommendation).
endometriosis-9.displayText: It is recommended to offer women hormone treatment (combined hormonal contraceptives, progestogens, GnRH agonists or GnRH antagonists) as one of the options to reduce endometriosis-associated pain. (Strong)

endometriosis-10.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-10.sourceText: When appropriate a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system or an etonogestrel-releasing subdermal implant to reduce endometriosis-associated pain can be used. (Strong)
endometriosis-10.displayText: When appropriate a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system or an etonogestrel-releasing subdermal implant to reduce endometriosis-associated pain can be used. (Strong)

endometriosis-11.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-11.sourceText: It is recommended to prescribe women GnRH agonists to reduce endometriosis-associated pain, although evidence is limited regarding dosage or duration of treatment. (Strong)
endometriosis-11.displayText: It is recommended to prescribe women GnRH agonists to reduce endometriosis-associated pain, although evidence is limited regarding dosage or duration of treatment. (Strong)

endometriosis-12.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-12.sourceText: 2.2.4 Clinicians should consider prescribing combined hormonal add-back therapy alongside GnRH agonist therapy to prevent bone loss and hypoestrogenic symptoms ( moderate level of evidence, strong recommendation).
endometriosis-12.displayText: Clinicians should consider prescribing combined hormonal add-back therapy alongside GnRH agonist therapy to prevent bone loss and hypoestrogenic symptoms. (Strong)

endometriosis-13.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-13.sourceText: 2.2.5 In women with endometriosis-associated pain refractory to other medical or surgical treatment, it is recommended to prescribe aromatase inhibitors, as they reduce endometriosis-associated pain.
endometriosis-13.displayText: In women with endometriosis-associated pain refractory to other medical or surgical treatment, it is recommended to prescribe aromatase inhibitors as they reduce endometriosis-associated pain. (Strong)

endometriosis-14.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-14.sourceText: 49-53 2.3.4 When performing surgery in women with ovarian endometrioma, clinicians should perform cystectomy instead of drainage and coagulation, as cystectomy reduces recurrence of endometrioma and endometriosis-associated pain (low level of evidence, strong recommendation) .
endometriosis-14.displayText: When performing surgery in women with ovarian endometrioma, clinicians should perform cystectomy instead of drainage and coagulation. (Strong)

endometriosis-15.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-15.sourceText: 54-60 2.3.5 When performing surgery for ovarian endometrioma, specific caution should be used to minimize ovarian damage (very ow level of evidence, strong recommendation) .
endometriosis-15.displayText: When performing surgery for ovarian endometrioma, specific caution should be used to minimize ovarian damage. (Strong)

endometriosis-16.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-16.sourceText: 63, 66 2.3.10 Clinicians can consider hysterectomy (with or without removal of the ovaries) with removal of all visible endometriosis lesions, in those women who no longer wish to conceive and failed to respond to more conservative treatments.
endometriosis-16.displayText: Clinicians can consider hysterectomy (with or without removal of the ovaries) with removal of all visible endometriosis lesions, in those women who no longer wish to conceive and failed to respond to more conservative treatments. (Conditional)

endometriosis-17.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-17.sourceText: Treatment of endometriosis associated infertility 3.1 Ovarian suppression 3.1.1 In infertile women with endometriosis, clinicians should not prescribe ovarian suppression treatment to improve fertility ( low level of evidence, strong recommendation ).
endometriosis-17.displayText: In infertile women with endometriosis, clinicians should not prescribe ovarian suppression treatment to improve fertility. (Strong)

endometriosis-18.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-18.sourceText: 3.4 Medically assisted reproduction 3.4.1 Intrauterine insemination in women with endometriosis 3.4.1.1 In infertile women with rASRM stage I/II endometriosis, clinicians may perform intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation, instead of expectant management or IUI alone, as it increases pregnancy rates (very low level of evidence, conditional recommendation).
endometriosis-18.displayText: In infertile women with rASRM stage I/II endometriosis, clinicians may perform intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation instead of expectant management or IUI alone, as it increases pregnancy rates. (Conditional)

endometriosis-19.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-19.sourceText: 3.4.2.1 ART can be performed for infertility associated with endometriosis, especially if tubal function is compromised, if there is male factor infertility, in case of low EFI and/or if other treatments have failed ( low level of evidence, Conditional recommendation ).
endometriosis-19.displayText: ART can be performed for infertility associated with endometriosis, especially if tubal function is compromised, if there is male factor infertility, in case of low EFI and/or if other treatments have failed. (Conditional)

endometriosis-20.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-20.sourceText: The Endometriosis Fertility Index (EFI) should be used to identify patients that may benefit from ART after surgery as it is validated, reproducible and cost-effective. (GPS)
endometriosis-20.displayText: The Endometriosis Fertility Index (EFI) should be used to identify patients that may benefit from ART after surgery as it is validated, reproducible and cost-effective. (GPS)

endometriosis-21.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-21.sourceText: 3.4.6 Fertility preservation 3.4.6.1 In case of extensive ovarian endometriosis, clinicians should discuss the pros and cons of fertility preservation with women with endometriosis.
endometriosis-21.displayText: In case of extensive ovarian endometriosis, clinicians should discuss the pros and cons of fertility preservation with women with endometriosis. (Strong)

endometriosis-22.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-22.sourceText: Clinicians should be aware that there may be an increased risk of first trimester miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy in women with endometriosis ( low level of evidence, strong recommendation ).
endometriosis-22.displayText: Clinicians should be aware that there may be an increased risk of first trimester miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy in women with endometriosis. (Strong)

endometriosis-23.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-23.sourceText: 10, 120, 122-125 4.1.3 After surgical management of ovarian endometrioma in women not immediately seeking conception, clinicians are recommended to offer long-term hormone treatment (e.g. combined hormonal contraceptives) for the secondary prevention of endometrioma and endometriosis-associated related symptom recurrence (very low level of evidence, strong recommendation ).
endometriosis-23.displayText: After surgical management of ovarian endometrioma in women not immediately seeking conception, clinicians are recommended to offer long-term hormone treatment (e.g. combined hormonal contraceptives) for the secondary prevention of endometrioma and endometriosis-associated related symptom recurrence. (Strong)

endometriosis-24.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-24.sourceText: cyclical pelvic pain (very low level of evidence, strong recommendation).
endometriosis-24.displayText: In adolescents, clinicians should take a careful history and consider the following symptoms as suggestive of the presence of endometriosis: chronic or a-cyclical pelvic pain, particularly combined with nausea, dysmenorrhea, dyschezia, dysuria, dyspareunia, and cyclical pelvic pain. (Strong)

endometriosis-25.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-25.sourceText: 5.6 Medical treatment 5.6.1 Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs should be the mainstay of pain relief for adolescents with endometriosis (GPS).
endometriosis-25.displayText: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs should be the mainstay of pain relief for adolescents with endometriosis. (GPS)

endometriosis-26.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-26.sourceText: 10 5.6.2 In adolescents with severe dysmenorrhea and/or endometriosis-associated pain, Clinicians should prescribe hormonal contraceptives or progestogens ( very low level of evidence, strong recommendation ).
endometriosis-26.displayText: In adolescents with severe dysmenorrhea and/or endometriosis-associated pain, clinicians should prescribe hormonal contraceptives or progestogens. (Strong)

endometriosis-27.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-27.sourceText: 10, 155, 156 6.2.2 Clinicians should avoid prescribing estrogen-only regimens for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal women with a history of endometriosis, as these regimens may be associated with a higher risk of malignant transformation ( low level of evidence, strong recommendation).
