endometriosis-27.displayText: Clinicians should avoid prescribing estrogen-only regimens for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms in postmenopausal women with a history of endometriosis, as these regimens may be associated with a higher risk of malignant transformation. (Strong)

endometriosis-28.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-28.sourceText: 6.3 Menopause-related major health concerns in women with endometriosis 6.3.1 Clinicians should be aware that women with endometriosis who have undergone an early bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy as part of their treatment have an increased risk of diminished bone density, dementia, and cardiovascular disease.
endometriosis-28.displayText: Clinicians should be aware that women with endometriosis who have undergone an early bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy as part of their treatment have an increased risk of diminished bone density, dementia, and cardiovascular disease. (GPS)

endometriosis-29.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-29.sourceText: 10 8.2 Clinicians should not routinely perform surgical excision/ablation for an incidental finding of asymptomatic endometriosis at the time of surgery ( very low level of evidence, strong recommendation ) .
endometriosis-29.displayText: Clinicians should not routinely perform surgical excision/ablation for an incidental finding of asymptomatic endometriosis at the time of surgery. (Strong)

endometriosis-30.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-30.sourceText: This recommendation is based on possible risk of persistent endometriosis and adenomyosis within the retained cervix and/or adjacent to it ( GPS).
endometriosis-30.displayText: This recommendation is based on possible risk of persistent endometriosis and adenomyosis within the retained cervix and/or adjacent to it. (GPS)

endometriosis-31.bookTitle: The diagnosis and management of endometriosis
endometriosis-31.sourceText: Extra pelvic endometriosis 7.1 Clinicians should be aware of symptoms of extra-pelvic thoracic endometriosis, such as cyclical shoulder pain, cyclical spontaneous pneumothorax, cyclical cough, or nodules which enlarge during menses. ( GPS).
endometriosis-31.displayText: Clinicians should be aware of symptoms of extra-pelvic thoracic endometriosis, such as cyclical shoulder pain, cyclical spontaneous pneumothorax, cyclical cough, or nodules which enlarge during menses. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-0.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-0.sourceText: 1.1.1. Discuss the benefits and risks of both caesarean and vaginal birth with women, taking into account their circumstances, concerns, priorities and plans for future pregnancies. (See Appendix I)
primary-cesarean-prevention-0.displayText: Discuss the benefits and risks of both caesarean and vaginal birth with women, taking into account their circumstances, concerns, priorities and plans for future pregnancies. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-1.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-1.sourceText: 1.1.2. Fetal presentation should be assessed and documented beginning at 36 0/7 weeks of gestation to guide the plan of management.
primary-cesarean-prevention-1.displayText: Fetal presentation should be assessed and documented beginning at 36 0/7 weeks of gestation to guide the plan of management. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-2.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-2.sourceText: the woman is in established labor
primary-cesarean-prevention-2.displayText: Offer women who have an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy after 36+0 weeks external cephalic version by an experienced obstetrician, unless the woman is in established labor, there is fetal compromise, the woman has ruptured membranes or vaginal bleeding, or the woman has other medical conditions that would make external cephalic version inadvisable. (Conditional)

primary-cesarean-prevention-3.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-3.sourceText: Before carrying out a caesarean birth for an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy, carry out an ultrasound scan to check that the baby is in the breech position as late as possible before the caesarean birth procedure. (GPS)
primary-cesarean-prevention-3.displayText: Before carrying out a caesarean birth for an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy, carry out an ultrasound scan to check that the baby is in the breech position as late as possible before the caesarean birth procedure. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-4.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-4.sourceText: 1.3.1 Cesarean delivery to avoid potential birth trauma should be limited to estimated fetal weights of at least 4500 g in women without diabetes and at least 4000 g in women with diabetes.
primary-cesarean-prevention-4.displayText: Cesarean delivery to avoid potential birth trauma should be limited to estimated fetal weights of at least 4500 g in women without diabetes and at least 4000 g in women with diabetes. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-5.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-5.sourceText: Perinatal outcomes for twin gestations in which first twin is in cephalic presentation are not improved by cesarean delivery. Thus, women with either cephalic/cephalic presenting twins or cephalic/non-cephalic presenting twins should be counseled to attempt vaginal delivery. (Strong)
primary-cesarean-prevention-5.displayText: Perinatal outcomes for twin gestations in which first twin is in cephalic presentation are not improved by cesarean delivery. Thus, women with either cephalic/cephalic presenting twins or cephalic/non-cephalic presenting twins should be counseled to attempt vaginal delivery. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-6.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-6.sourceText: 1.5.1. Do not use pelvimetry for decision making about mode of birth.
primary-cesarean-prevention-6.displayText: Do not use pelvimetry for decision making about mode of birth. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-7.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-7.sourceText: estimations of fetal size (ultrasound or clinical examination).
primary-cesarean-prevention-7.displayText: Do not use maternal shoe size, maternal height, or estimations of fetal size to predict cephalopelvic disproportion. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-8.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-8.sourceText: 1.6.1 Hepatitis B virus: Do not offer pregnant women with hepatitis B a planned caesarean birth for this reason alone, as mother-to-baby transmission of hepatitis B can be reduced if the baby receives immunoglobulin and vaccination.
primary-cesarean-prevention-8.displayText: Do not offer pregnant women with hepatitis B a planned caesarean birth for this reason alone, as mother-to-baby transmission of hepatitis B can be reduced if the baby receives immunoglobulin and vaccination. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-9.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-9.sourceText: 1.6.2 Hepatitis C virus: Do not offer women who are infected with hepatitis C a planned caesarean birth for this reason alone.
primary-cesarean-prevention-9.displayText: Do not offer women who are infected with hepatitis C a planned caesarean birth for this reason alone. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-10.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-10.sourceText: 1.7.1. Do not use a BMI of over 50 kg/m2 alone as an indication for planned caesarean birth.
primary-cesarean-prevention-10.displayText: Do not use a BMI of over 50 kg/m2 alone as an indication for planned caesarean birth. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-11.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-11.sourceText: discuss and explore the reasons for the request
primary-cesarean-prevention-11.displayText: If a pregnant woman with no medical indication for a caesarean birth requests a caesarean birth, discuss and explore the reasons for the request, address concerns about pain and pain relief options, discuss the overall benefits and risks of CS compared with vaginal birth, and document the discussion and the decision taken. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-12.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-12.sourceText: 1.8.2. Don t do cesarean section on request without a written informed consent from the woman indicating that this is a CS on request in absence of a medical or obstetric indication.
primary-cesarean-prevention-12.displayText: Don't do cesarean section on request without a written informed consent from the woman indicating that this is a CS on request in absence of a medical or obstetric indication. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-13.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-13.sourceText: 1.9.1 Non-engagement of the head in a primigravida should not be considered as an only factor requiring cesarean birth.
primary-cesarean-prevention-13.displayText: Non-engagement of the head in a primigravida should not be considered as an only factor requiring cesarean birth. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-14.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-14.sourceText: 2.1.1. Before 41 0/7 weeks of gestation, induction of labor generally should be performed based on maternal and fetal medical indications. Inductions at 41 0/7 weeks of gestation should be performed to reduce risk of cesarean delivery and risk of perinatal morbidity and mortality.
primary-cesarean-prevention-14.displayText: Before 41 0/7 weeks of gestation, induction of labor generally should be performed based on maternal and fetal medical indications. Inductions at ≥ 41 0/7 weeks of gestation should be performed to reduce risk of cesarean delivery and risk of perinatal morbidity and mortality. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-15.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-15.sourceText: 2.1.2 Cervical ripening methods should be used when labor is induced in women with unfavorable cervix.
primary-cesarean-prevention-15.displayText: Cervical ripening methods should be used when labor is induced in women with unfavorable cervix. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-16.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-16.sourceText: 2.2.2 A prolonged latent phase (eg, 20 hours in nulliparous women and 14 hours in multiparous women) should not be an indication for cesarean delivery.
primary-cesarean-prevention-16.displayText: A prolonged latent phase (eg, >20 hours in nulliparous women and >14 hours in multiparous women) should not be an indication for cesarean delivery. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-17.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-17.sourceText: 2.3.7. Labor may not naturally accelerate until a cervical dilatation threshold of 5 cm is reached. Therefore, the use of medical interventions to accelerate labor and birth (such as oxytocin augmentation or caesarean section) before this threshold is not recommended, provided fetal and maternal conditions are reassuring.
primary-cesarean-prevention-17.displayText: Labor may not naturally accelerate until a cervical dilatation threshold of 5 cm is reached. Therefore, the use of medical interventions to accelerate labor and birth (such as oxytocin augmentation or caesarean section) before this threshold is not recommended, provided fetal and maternal conditions are reassuring. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-18.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-18.sourceText: 2.3.2 Use a partogram with a 4-hour action line to monitor progress of women in spontaneous labor with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy at term starting in the active phase, to reduce the likelihood of caesarean birth.
primary-cesarean-prevention-18.displayText: Use a partogram with a 4-hour action line to monitor progress of women in spontaneous labor with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy at term starting in the active phase, to reduce the likelihood of caesarean birth. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-19.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-19.sourceText: 2.3.3. Regarding the Partogram : A minimum cervical dilatation rate of 1 cm/hour throughout active first stage is not recommended for identification of normal labor progression and a slower than 1-cm/hour cervical dilatation rate alone should not be a routine indication for obstetric intervention.
primary-cesarean-prevention-19.displayText: A minimum cervical dilatation rate of 1 cm/hour throughout active first stage is not recommended for identification of normal labor progression and a slower than 1-cm/hour cervical dilatation rate alone should not be a routine indication for obstetric intervention. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-20.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-20.sourceText: 2.3.4. A cervical dilatation of 0.5 cm per hour (2 cm in 4 hours) is considered normal in the active phase.
primary-cesarean-prevention-20.displayText: A cervical dilatation of 0.5 cm per hour (2 cm in 4 hours) is considered normal in the active phase. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-21.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-21.sourceText: consider amniotomy if membranes are intact,
primary-cesarean-prevention-21.displayText: For women with intact membranes in whom delay in the established first stage of labor is confirmed, consider amniotomy if membranes are intact and oxytocin if inertia was diagnosed, then repeat a vaginal examination 2 hours later. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-22.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-22.sourceText: If oxytocin is used, ensure that the time between increments of the dose is no more frequent than every 30 minutes and increase oxytocin until there are 4 5 contractions in 10 minutes.
primary-cesarean-prevention-22.displayText: If oxytocin is used, ensure that the time between increments of the dose is no more frequent than every 30 minutes and increase oxytocin until there are 4-5 contractions in 10 minutes. (GPS)

primary-cesarean-prevention-23.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-23.sourceText: 2.3.8. Arrest in labor (complete cessation of progress) is diagnosed at cervical dilatation of 6 cm or more with ruptured membranes and no or limited cervical change for 4 hours of adequate contractions.
primary-cesarean-prevention-23.displayText: Arrest in labor (complete cessation of progress) is diagnosed at cervical dilatation of 6 cm or more with ruptured membranes and no or limited cervical change for 4 hours of adequate contractions. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-24.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-24.sourceText: Cesarean delivery for active-phase arrest in first stage of labor should be reserved for women ≥ 6 cm of dilation with ruptured membranes who fail to progress despite 4 hours of adequate uterine activity. (Strong)
primary-cesarean-prevention-24.displayText: Cesarean delivery for active-phase arrest in first stage of labor should be reserved for women ≥ 6 cm of dilation with ruptured membranes who fail to progress despite 4 hours of adequate uterine activity. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-25.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-25.sourceText: 2.4.1. Intermittent auscultation of the fetal heart rate with either a Doppler ultrasound device or Pinard fetal stethoscope is recommended for healthy pregnant women in labor.
primary-cesarean-prevention-25.displayText: Intermittent auscultation of the fetal heart rate with either a Doppler ultrasound device or Pinard fetal stethoscope is recommended for healthy pregnant women in labor. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-26.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-26.sourceText: Auscultate the fetal heart rate every 15-30 minutes in active first stage of labor and every 5 minutes in the second stage, for at least 1 minute during and 30 seconds after a uterine contraction. (Strong)
primary-cesarean-prevention-26.displayText: Auscultate the fetal heart rate every 15-30 minutes in active first stage of labor and every 5 minutes in the second stage, for at least 1 minute during and 30 seconds after a uterine contraction. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-27.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-27.sourceText: At least 1 h of pushing in multiparous women
primary-cesarean-prevention-27.displayText: Before diagnosing arrest of labor in second stage, if maternal and fetal conditions permit, allow at least 1 h of pushing in multiparous women and at least 2 h of pushing in nulliparous women. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-28.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-28.sourceText: 2.5.6. Operative vaginal delivery in second stage of labor by experienced and well-trained physicians should be considered safe, acceptable alternative to cesarean delivery. Training in, and ongoing maintenance of, practical skills related to operative vaginal delivery should be encouraged.
primary-cesarean-prevention-28.displayText: Operative vaginal delivery in second stage of labor by experienced and well-trained physicians should be considered safe, acceptable alternative to cesarean delivery. Training in, and ongoing maintenance of, practical skills related to operative vaginal delivery should be encouraged. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-29.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-29.sourceText: Offer women who have an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy after 36 0 weeks, external cephalic version (ECV) by an experienced obstetrician. (Strong)
primary-cesarean-prevention-29.displayText: Offer women who have an uncomplicated singleton breech pregnancy after 36 0 weeks, external cephalic version (ECV) by an experienced obstetrician. (Strong)

primary-cesarean-prevention-30.bookTitle: Recommendations on The Clinical Interventions For The Prevention of The Primary Cesarean Section
primary-cesarean-prevention-30.sourceText: This guideline offers evidence-based recommendations on the clinical interventions for the safe prevention of the primary cesarean section. The recommendations are intended to provide healthcare professionals caring for pregnant women with practical guidance on how to safely avoid the primary cesarean section.
primary-cesarean-prevention-30.displayText: This guideline offers evidence-based recommendations on the clinical interventions for the safe prevention of the primary cesarean section. (Strong)

pph-0.sourceText: Risk factors for PPH may present antenatally or intrapartum; care plans must be modified as and when risk factors arise. (GPS)
pph-0.displayText: Risk factors for PPH may present antenatally or intrapartum; care plans must be modified as and when risk factors arise. (GPS)

pph-1.sourceText: - Women with known risk factors for PPH should only be delivered in a hospital with a blood bank on site. (Strong, low) 5
pph-1.displayText: Women with known risk factors for PPH should only be delivered in a hospital with a blood bank on site. (Strong)

pph-2.sourceText: - An individualized risk assessment for postpartum hemorrhage should be documented upon arrival to a labor unit and updated throughout labor and delivery. (Strong, low) 5
pph-2.displayText: An individualized risk assessment for postpartum hemorrhage should be documented upon arrival to a labor unit and updated throughout labor and delivery. (Strong)

pph-3.sourceText: Previous Cesarean section with placenta previa or PAS
pph-3.displayText: Antenatal risk factors for PPH include: Age > 35, Obesity (BMI >35), More than 3 prior births, Previous PPH, Previous Cesarean section with placenta previa or PAS, Previous uterine surgery, Uterine fibroid, Multiple pregnancy, Polyhydramnios, Fetal macrosomia, Anemia, Known coagulopathy or other bleeding disorders. (GPS)

pph-4.displayText: Intrapartum risk factors for PPH include: Oxytocin use in labor, Prolonged second stage, Prolonged third stage, Retained placenta, Manual removal of placenta, Assisted vaginal birth, Cesarean section, Perineal trauma, Uterine rupture, General anaesthesia, Infection, Non-cephalic presentation, Precipitate labor. (GPS)

pph-5.sourceText: Antenatal anemia should be investigated and treated appropriately as this may reduce the morbidity associated with PPH. (Strong)
pph-5.displayText: Antenatal anemia should be investigated and treated appropriately as this may reduce the morbidity associated with PPH. (Strong)

pph-6.sourceText: - The use of uterotonics for prevention of PPH during the third stage of labor is recommended for all births. (strong, high) 10,15
pph-6.displayText: The use of uterotonics for prevention of PPH during the third stage of labor is recommended for all births. (Strong)

pph-7.sourceText: 1.4.2.1. Late cord clamping (performed approximately 1 to 3 minutes after birth) is recommended for all births while initiating simultaneous essential newborn care. (strong, moderate) 16
pph-7.displayText: Late cord clamping (performed approximately 1 to 3 minutes after birth) is recommended for all births while initiating simultaneous essential newborn care. (Strong)

pph-8.sourceText: 1.4.2.2. Early cord clamping ( 1 minute after birth) is not recommended unless the neonate is asphyxiated and needs to be moved immediately for resuscitation. (strong, moderate) 16
pph-8.displayText: Early cord clamping (<1 minute after birth) is not recommended unless the neonate is asphyxiated and needs to be moved immediately for resuscitation. (Strong)

pph-9.sourceText: - Consider Controlled cord traction (CCT) as part of active/modified active management of third stage. (strong, low) 17
pph-9.displayText: Consider Controlled cord traction (CCT) as part of active/modified active management of third stage. (Strong)

pph-10.sourceText: o In most circumstances, oxytocin is the prophylactic uterotonic of choice. 9,18
pph-10.displayText: In most circumstances, oxytocin is the prophylactic uterotonic of choice. (Strong)

pph-11.sourceText: For vaginal birth with IV access: Oxytocin 10 IU IV injected slowly over 3-5 minutes is recommended in preference to IM. If vaginal birth without IV access: Oxytocin 10 IU IM. (Strong)
pph-11.displayText: For vaginal birth with IV access: Oxytocin 10 IU IV injected slowly over 3-5 minutes is recommended in preference to IM. If vaginal birth without IV access: Oxytocin 10 IU IM. (Strong)

pph-12.sourceText: For CS birth: Oxytocin 5 IU IV over 1-2 minutes, monitor for hemodynamic impact, avoid rapid IV bolus administration. (Strong)
pph-12.displayText: For CS birth: Oxytocin 5 IU IV over 1-2 minutes, monitor for hemodynamic impact, avoid rapid IV bolus administration. (Strong)

pph-13.sourceText: Ergometrine can be given IM or, in life-saving circumstances, as a slow IV injection. Ergometrine should not be used in patients with essential or gestational hypertension, or in patients on HIV protease inhibitors. (Conditional)
pph-13.displayText: Ergometrine can be given IM or, in life-saving circumstances, as a slow IV injection. Ergometrine should not be used in patients with essential or gestational hypertension, or in patients on HIV protease inhibitors. (Conditional)

pph-14.sourceText: o Routinely use oxytocin in preference to carbetocin if vaginal birth and cold-chain storage of oxytocin can be guaranteed (e.g. hospital setting). 18,26
pph-14.displayText: Routinely use oxytocin in preference to carbetocin if vaginal birth and cold-chain storage of oxytocin can be guaranteed (e.g. hospital setting). (Conditional)

pph-15.sourceText: Misoprostol is not recommended if alternative injectable uterotonics are available; use only if no other injectable uterotonic is available. The dose is 600 micrograms orally or sublingual single dose immediately after birth. (Conditional)
pph-15.displayText: Misoprostol is not recommended if alternative injectable uterotonics are available; use only if no other injectable uterotonic is available. The dose is 600 micrograms orally or sublingual single dose immediately after birth. (Conditional)

pph-16.sourceText: Tranexamic acid can be used as a prophylactic agent as an adjunct to uterotonics in patients at high risk for postpartum hemorrhage. Use TXA within 3 hours of birth in a fixed dose of 1 g in 10 mL IV over 10 minutes. (Strong)
pph-16.displayText: Tranexamic acid can be used as a prophylactic agent as an adjunct to uterotonics in patients at high risk for postpartum hemorrhage. Use TXA within 3 hours of birth in a fixed dose of 1 g in 10 mL IV over 10 minutes. (Strong)

pph-17.sourceText: PPH defined as blood loss ≥500ml after vaginal birth or ≥1000ml after cesarean section within 24 hours.
pph-17.displayText: PPH defined as blood loss ≥500ml after vaginal birth or ≥1000ml after cesarean section within 24 hours.

pph-18.sourceText: PPH can be minor (500-1000 ml blood loss) or major (more than 1000 ml blood loss). The condition becomes worse if the patient lost >2000 mL of blood. (GPS)
pph-18.displayText: PPH can be minor (500-1000 ml blood loss) or major (more than 1000 ml blood loss). The condition becomes worse if the patient lost >2000 mL of blood. (GPS)

pph-19.sourceText: - Diagnose minor PPH (blood loss 500-1000 mL) if there are: (GPS)
pph-19.displayText: Diagnose minor PPH (blood loss 500-1000 mL) if there are: Normal blood pressure, Mild increase in heart rate (but <100 beats/minute), Palpitation, Lightheadedness. (GPS)

pph-20.sourceText: - Diagnose major PPH (blood loss from 1000-2000 mL) if there are: (GPS)
pph-20.displayText: Diagnose major PPH (blood loss from 1000-2000 mL) if there are: Drop of blood pressure below the original average of the patient, Tachycardia (≥ 100 beats/minute), Sweating, Weakness. (GPS)

pph-21.sourceText: - Be aware that signs of hemodynamic compromise are a late indicator of PPH and may not be evident until large volumes of blood are lost (e.g. up to 25% of total blood volume or greater than 1500 mL). (Strong, moderate) 40
pph-21.displayText: Signs of hemodynamic compromise are a late indicator of PPH and may not be evident until large volumes of blood are lost (e.g. up to 25% of total blood volume or greater than 1500 mL). (GPS)

pph-22.sourceText: 3.1.4. The GDG recommends adoption of the EMOTIVE bundle (Early detection, Massage, Oxytocics, Tranexamic acid, IV fluids, Examination Escalation) as the standard first-response protocol for all cases of postpartum hemorrhage. Initiate all components within 15 minutes of PPH diagnosis to ensure rapid, standardized, and evidence-based management, with ongoing monitoring and escalation as needed, see Appendix I. (Strong, low) 10
pph-22.displayText: The GDG recommends adoption of the EMOTIVE bundle (Early detection, Massage, Oxytocics, Tranexamic acid, IV fluids, Examination & Escalation) as the standard first-response protocol for all cases of postpartum hemorrhage. Initiate all components within 15 minutes of PPH diagnosis. (Strong)

pph-23.sourceText: If blood loss after delivery seems increased, assess for the Tone of the uterus, the presence of Trauma, any retained Tissue or Thrombin activity (the 4Ts). (GPS)
pph-23.displayText: If blood loss after delivery seems increased, assess for the Tone of the uterus, the presence of Trauma, any retained Tissue or Thrombin activity (the 4Ts). (GPS)

pph-24.displayText: Full protocol for major PPH: Assess airway and breathing, evaluate circulation, position the patient flat, insert two peripheral cannulas (14 gauge), draw 20 mL of blood for cross-matching, FBC, coagulation screen and chemistry profile, keep the woman warm, transfuse blood as soon as possible. (GPS)

pph-25.sourceText: Provide emergency blood (Packed RBCs) with immediate issue of group O, rhesus D (RhD)-negative with a switch to group-specific blood as soon as feasible. (GPS)
pph-25.displayText: Provide emergency blood (Packed RBCs) with immediate issue of group O, rhesus D (RhD)-negative with a switch to group-specific blood as soon as feasible. (GPS)

pph-26.sourceText: After 4 units of red blood cells, 4 units of FFP should be infused until test results are known, if bleeding is continuing and coagulation profile results are not available. (GPS)
pph-26.displayText: After 4 units of red blood cells, 4 units of FFP should be infused until test results are known, if bleeding is continuing and coagulation profile results are not available. (GPS)

pph-27.sourceText: Cryoprecipitate should be used for fibrinogen replacement.
pph-27.displayText: A plasma fibrinogen level of greater than 2 g/l should be maintained during ongoing PPH. Cryoprecipitate should be used for fibrinogen replacement. (GPS)

pph-28.sourceText: During PPH, platelets should be transfused when the platelet count is less than 75 10 9 /l (75000 / mm 3 ) based on laboratory monitoring. (GPS)
pph-28.displayText: During PPH, platelets should be transfused when the platelet count is less than 75 ×10^9/l. (GPS)

pph-29.displayText: Maintain the following lab parameters: Hb greater than 8 gm%, Platelet count greater than 50 ×10^9/l, PT less than 1.5 times normal, APTT less than 1.5 times normal, Fibrinogen level greater than 2 g/l. (GPS)

pph-30.sourceText: Tranexamic acid can be used in all patients as an adjunct to uterotonics in the setting of postpartum hemorrhage regardless of whether the bleeding is due to genital tract trauma or other causes. Give TXA as early as possible within 3 hours of birth, 1 g in 10 mL IV at 1 mL per minute. (Strong)
pph-30.displayText: Tranexamic acid can be used in all patients as an adjunct to uterotonics in the setting of postpartum hemorrhage regardless of whether the bleeding is due to genital tract trauma or other causes. Give TXA as early as possible within 3 hours of birth, 1 g in 10 mL IV at 1 mL per minute. (Strong)

pph-31.sourceText: The most common cause of primary PPH is uterine atony. The initial management of PPH should involve measures to stimulate myometrial contractions. (GPS)
pph-31.displayText: The most common cause of primary PPH is uterine atony. The initial management of PPH should involve measures to stimulate myometrial contractions. (GPS)

pph-32.sourceText: First line pharmacological therapy for uterine atony (Oxytocin): Give oxytocin 5 IU IV over 1-2 minutes; continue with oxytocin IV infusion 40 IU in 500 mL at a rate of 5-10 IU/hour for a minimum of 2-4 hours. (GPS)
pph-32.displayText: First line pharmacological therapy for uterine atony (Oxytocin): Give oxytocin 5 IU IV over 1-2 minutes; continue with oxytocin IV infusion 40 IU in 500 mL at a rate of 5-10 IU/hour for a minimum of 2-4 hours. (GPS)

pph-33.sourceText: Ergometrine maleate 0.25-0.5 mg IV over 1-2 minutes may be repeated every 5 minutes to a maximum of 1 mg. It is contraindicated with retained placenta, severe hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, severe/persistent sepsis, renal, hepatic, vascular, or cardiac disease. (GPS)
pph-33.displayText: Ergometrine maleate 0.25-0.5 mg IV over 1-2 minutes may be repeated every 5 minutes to a maximum of 1 mg. It is contraindicated with retained placenta, severe hypertension, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, severe/persistent sepsis, renal, hepatic, vascular, or cardiac disease. (GPS)

pph-34.sourceText: - Give 800 mcg sublingual (rapid onset of action with side effects more likely)
pph-34.displayText: Consider misoprostol if alternative uterotonics unavailable or contraindicated (e.g. asthma, hypertension). Give 800 mcg sublingual or 1000 mcg per rectum. (GPS)

pph-35.sourceText: - Bimanual Compression: The use of bimanual uterine compression is recommended as a temporary measure until appropriate care is available for the treatment of PPH due to uterine atony after vaginal delivery (Strong, low) 10
pph-35.displayText: The use of bimanual uterine compression is recommended as a temporary measure until appropriate care is available for the treatment of PPH due to uterine atony after vaginal delivery. (Strong)

pph-36.sourceText: Consider the use of intrauterine balloon tamponade (e.g. Bakri Balloon) as balloon is an appropriate first-line surgical intervention for most women where uterine atony is the only or main cause of hemorrhage after the success of bimanual uterine compression. (Strong)
pph-36.displayText: Consider the use of intrauterine balloon tamponade (e.g. Bakri Balloon) as balloon is an appropriate first-line surgical intervention for most women where uterine atony is the only or main cause of hemorrhage after the success of bimanual uterine compression. (Strong)

pph-37.sourceText: - Consider B-Lynch compression or other compression suture. (GPS)
pph-37.displayText: Consider B-Lynch compression or other compression suture. (GPS)

pph-38.displayText: Stepwise arterial ligation for uterine devascularization: Bilateral uterine artery ligation, bilateral utero-ovarian artery ligation, and if expertise available, bilateral internal iliac artery ligation. (GPS)

pph-39.sourceText: Resort to hysterectomy early (sooner rather than later) especially if life is threatened, bleeding continues after use of conservative treatment options, or blood transfusion is limited or not an option. (Strong)
pph-39.displayText: Resort to hysterectomy early (sooner rather than later) especially if life is threatened, bleeding continues after use of conservative treatment options, or blood transfusion is limited or not an option. (Strong)

pph-40.sourceText: 8.8.2. Subtotal (Supra-Vaginal) hysterectomy is quicker and safer in Major PPH and in packing of the abdomen, use hot packs (GPS)
pph-40.displayText: Subtotal (Supra-Vaginal) hysterectomy is quicker and safer in Major PPH. (GPS)

pph-41.sourceText: - Every maternity unit should have a multidisciplinary protocol for the management of PPH. (GPS)
pph-41.displayText: Every maternity unit should have a multidisciplinary protocol for the management of PPH. (GPS)

pph-42.sourceText: - All cases of PPH involving a blood loss of greater than 1500 ml should be the subject of a formal clinical incident review. (GPS)
pph-42.displayText: All cases of PPH involving a blood loss of greater than 1500 ml should be the subject of a formal clinical incident review. (GPS)

pph-43.sourceText: Ensure that the bladder is empty (Foley catheter leave in place) to monitor urine output during resuscitation and management of PPH. (GPS)
pph-43.displayText: Ensure that the bladder is empty (Foley catheter leave in place) to monitor urine output during resuscitation and management of PPH. (GPS)

pph-44.sourceText: Sustained uterine massage is not recommended as an intervention to prevent PPH in women who have received prophylactic oxytocin; bimanual uterine compression is recommended for active hemorrhage. (Strong)
pph-44.displayText: Sustained uterine massage is not recommended as an intervention to prevent PPH in women who have received prophylactic oxytocin; bimanual uterine compression is recommended for active hemorrhage. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-0.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-0.sourceText: NVP is diagnosed when onset is prior to 16 weeks of gestation and other causes of nausea and vomiting have been excluded
nausea-vomiting-0.displayText: NVP is diagnosed when onset is prior to 16 weeks of gestation and other causes of nausea and vomiting have been excluded. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-1.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-1.sourceText: HG is diagnosed when symptoms start in early pregnancy, nausea and/or vomiting are severe enough to cause an inability to eat and drink normally and strongly limits daily activities of living (see the differential diagnosis of NVP in appendix).
nausea-vomiting-1.displayText: HG is diagnosed when symptoms start in early pregnancy, nausea and/or vomiting are severe enough to cause an inability to eat and drink normally and strongly limits daily activities of living. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-2.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-2.sourceText: An objective and validated index of nausea and vomiting such as the PUQE tool can be used to classify the severity of NVP and HG. (Conditional)
nausea-vomiting-2.displayText: An objective and validated index of nausea and vomiting such as the PUQE tool can be used to classify the severity of NVP and HG. (Conditional)

nausea-vomiting-3.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-3.sourceText: Ketonuria is not an indicator of dehydration in pregnancy and should not be used to assess severity. Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence (8)
nausea-vomiting-3.displayText: Ketonuria is not an indicator of dehydration in pregnancy and should not be used to assess severity. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-4.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-4.sourceText: Avoid an empty stomach at all times, with small and frequent meals every 1-2h. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-4.displayText: Avoid an empty stomach at all times, with small and frequent meals every 1-2h. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-5.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-5.sourceText: Prevent a full stomach (ie. not mixing solid with liquid, avoiding large meals). (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-5.displayText: Prevent a full stomach (ie. not mixing solid with liquid, avoiding large meals). (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-6.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-6.sourceText: Eat dry food, high-protein snacks, and crackers in the morning before arising. Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence (11)
nausea-vomiting-6.displayText: Eat dry food, high-protein snacks, and crackers in the morning before arising. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-7.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-7.sourceText: Avoid strong tasting and spicy food, eliminate supplemental iron. Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence (11)
nausea-vomiting-7.displayText: Avoid strong tasting and spicy food, eliminate supplemental iron. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-8.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-8.sourceText: Ginger, has shown a beneficial effect in reducing nausea symptoms, but not in reducing vomiting. Strong recommendation, high quality evidence (11)
nausea-vomiting-8.displayText: Ginger has shown a beneficial effect in reducing nausea symptoms, but not in reducing vomiting. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-9.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-9.sourceText: We recommend against acupuncture, acupressure and hypnosis. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-9.displayText: We recommend against acupuncture, acupressure and hypnosis. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-10.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-10.sourceText: Doxylamine/pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is recommended as the first-line therapy for mild-moderate NVP: Doxylamine/pyridoxine 20/20mg PO at night, increase additional 10/10 mg in morning and 10/10mg at lunchtime if required.
nausea-vomiting-10.displayText: Doxylamine/pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is recommended as the first-line therapy for mild-moderate NVP: Doxylamine/pyridoxine 20/20mg PO at night, increase additional 10/10 mg in morning and 10/10mg at lunchtime if required. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-11.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-11.sourceText: If no adequate response to first-line therapy, add antihistaminic: Cyclizine 50 mg PO, IM or IV 8 hourly, or Promethazine 12.5-25 mg 4-8 hourly PO, IM or IV. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-11.displayText: If no adequate response to first-line therapy, add antihistaminic: Cyclizine 50 mg PO, IM or IV 8 hourly, or Promethazine 12.5-25 mg 4-8 hourly PO, IM or IV. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-12.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-12.sourceText: If no adequate response, add dopamine antagonists: Prochlorperazine 5-10 mg 6-8 hourly PO (or 3 mg buccal); Metoclopramide 5-10 mg 8 hourly PO, IV/IM/SC; Domperidone 10 mg 8 hourly PO. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-12.displayText: If no adequate response, add dopamine antagonists: Prochlorperazine 5-10 mg 6-8 hourly PO (or 3 mg buccal); Metoclopramide 5-10 mg 8 hourly PO, IV/IM/SC; Domperidone 10 mg 8 hourly PO. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-13.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-13.sourceText: If no adequate response, add Ondansetron 4 mg 8 hourly or 8 mg 12 hourly PO; 8 mg over 15 minutes 12 hourly IV. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-13.displayText: If no adequate response, add Ondansetron 4 mg 8 hourly or 8 mg 12 hourly PO; 8 mg over 15 minutes 12 hourly IV. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-14.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-14.sourceText: If no adequate response, add Hydrocortisone 100 mg twice daily IV and once clinical improvement occurs convert to prednisolone 40-50 mg daily PO with gradual tapering. Corticosteroids should be reserved for cases where standard therapies have failed. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-14.displayText: If no adequate response, add Hydrocortisone 100 mg twice daily IV and once clinical improvement occurs convert to prednisolone 40-50 mg daily PO with gradual tapering. Corticosteroids should be reserved for cases where standard therapies have failed. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-15.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-15.sourceText: Acid-reducing agents can be used as adjunctive therapy. In patients with heartburn/acid reflux and NVP. Conditional recommendation, very low-quality evidence, (36)
nausea-vomiting-15.displayText: Acid-reducing agents can be used as adjunctive therapy in patients with heartburn/acid reflux and NVP. (Conditional)

nausea-vomiting-16.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-16.sourceText: - Hospital admission for close monitoring and ongoing treatment is appropriate for those with persistent inability to tolerate oral intake resulting in hypovolemia requiring intravenous replacement fluid, and failure of oral and/or intravenous antiemetic therapy. Strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence, (37)
nausea-vomiting-16.displayText: Hospital admission for close monitoring and ongoing treatment is appropriate for those with persistent inability to tolerate oral intake resulting in hypovolemia requiring intravenous replacement fluid. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-17.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-17.sourceText: Aggressively rehydrate with up to 2 liters of IV crystalloid over two hours (preferably with lactated Ringer's), then titrate IV fluids to maintain urine output at least 100 mL/hour. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-17.displayText: Aggressively rehydrate with up to 2 liters of IV crystalloid over two hours (preferably with lactated Ringer's), then titrate IV fluids to maintain urine output at least 100 mL/hour. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-18.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-18.sourceText: Thiamine should be administered before administering glucose.
nausea-vomiting-18.displayText: To reduce the risk of Wernicke encephalopathy, 100 to 200 mg thiamine (vitamin B1) should be added to the initial fluid resuscitation and then daily thereafter. Thiamine should be administered before administering glucose. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-19.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-19.sourceText: o Begin with ondansetron 4 mg intravenously (IV push) once every eight hours upon hospitalization for intravenous fluid therapy and may increase to 8 mg IV every eight hours. After the patient has stabilized, ondansetron is discontinued. Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence, (10) .
nausea-vomiting-19.displayText: Begin with ondansetron 4 mg intravenously (IV push) once every eight hours upon hospitalization for intravenous fluid therapy and may increase to 8 mg IV every eight hours. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-20.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-20.sourceText: Women admitted with HG should be offered thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparin and those being managed as outpatients should be assessed for VTE risk. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-20.displayText: Women admitted with HG should be offered thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparin and those being managed as outpatients should be assessed for VTE risk. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-21.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-21.sourceText: Consider testing for H. pylori infection in patients unresponsive to standard therapy, who have symptoms beyond the first trimester, or who require multiple hospitalizations. (Conditional)
nausea-vomiting-21.displayText: Consider testing for H. pylori infection in patients unresponsive to standard therapy, who have symptoms beyond the first trimester, or who require multiple hospitalizations. (Conditional)

nausea-vomiting-22.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-22.sourceText: When all other medical therapies have failed to sufficiently manage symptoms, enteral tube feeding or parenteral nutrition should be considered with a referral to a specialized physician. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-22.displayText: When all other medical therapies have failed to sufficiently manage symptoms, enteral tube feeding or parenteral nutrition should be considered with a referral to a specialized physician. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-23.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-23.sourceText: At the time of discharge, it is essential that women are advised to continue with their antiemetics for at least one week and that they know how to access further care. Strong recommendation, very-low quality evidence, (8)
nausea-vomiting-23.displayText: At the time of discharge, it is essential that women are advised to continue with their antiemetics for at least one week and that they know how to access further care. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-24.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-24.sourceText: Women with severe NVP or HG who have continued symptoms into the late second or the third trimester should be offered serial scans to monitor fetal growth, Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence, (8)
nausea-vomiting-24.displayText: Women with severe NVP or HG who have continued symptoms into the late second or the third trimester should be offered serial scans to monitor fetal growth. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-25.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-25.sourceText: Women who experience HG in pregnancy are at increased risk of PND, anxiety, and PTSD. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-25.displayText: Women who experience HG in pregnancy are at increased risk of PND, anxiety, and PTSD. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-26.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-26.sourceText: Women with previous HG should be advised that there is a risk of recurrence in future pregnancies. Strong recommendation, moderate quality evidence, (8)
nausea-vomiting-26.displayText: Women with previous HG should be advised that there is a risk of recurrence in future pregnancies. (Strong)

nausea-vomiting-27.bookTitle: The management of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy
nausea-vomiting-27.sourceText: Hospital admission for close monitoring and ongoing treatment is appropriate for those with persistent hyperemesis gravidarum and inability to tolerate oral intake resulting in hypovolemia. (Strong)
nausea-vomiting-27.displayText: Hospital admission for close monitoring and ongoing treatment is appropriate for those with persistent hyperemesis gravidarum and inability to tolerate oral intake resulting in hypovolemia. (Strong)

normal-labor-0.displayText: Normal labor is labor that: occurs between 37+0 and 42+0 completed weeks, spontaneous onset, singleton gestation, vertex presentation, normal labor progress, spontaneous vaginal birth, with no maternal or fetal complications or risk factors. (Strong)

normal-labor-1.displayText: This guideline offers evidence-based recommendations on diagnosis and management of normal labor and delivery to provide healthcare professionals with practical guidance on appropriate care and management of women in normal labor. (Strong)

normal-labor-2.displayText: The benefits of normal labor and birth for the woman and baby include: enhances labor effectiveness, promotes fetal readiness for birth, protects the baby from reduced oxygen during labor, improves physiological response to labor stress and pain, promotes maternal and newborn transitions, and minimizes maternal bleeding. (Strong)

normal-labor-3.sourceText: General Care and support for normal labor
normal-labor-3.displayText: General care and support for normal labor: explain to the woman that they should drink during labor when thirsty (isotonic drinks may be beneficial), maintain mobile positions, avoid supine position, and provide continuous one-to-one labor companionship. (Strong)

normal-labor-4.sourceText: Review history, pregnancy notes and screening results including:
normal-labor-4.displayText: Review history, pregnancy notes and screening results including gestational age, past history (medical, obstetric, gynecological, surgical, social, family), medications, allergies, pregnancy complications, and investigation results. (Strong)

normal-labor-5.sourceText: Ask her about the length, strength and frequency of her contractions
normal-labor-5.displayText: Ask her about the length, strength and frequency of her contractions, fetal movements in the last 24 hours, and vaginal losses. (Strong)

normal-labor-6.sourceText: Routine clinical pelvimetry on admission in labor is not recommended for healthy pregnant women.
normal-labor-6.displayText: Routine clinical pelvimetry on admission in labor is not recommended for healthy pregnant women. (Strong)

normal-labor-7.sourceText: Ruptured membranes and not in labor
normal-labor-7.displayText: Contraindication to vaginal examination: Antepartum hemorrhage, ruptured membranes and not in labor, placenta previa, placental position unknown, suspected preterm labor. (Strong)

normal-labor-8.displayText: Women with cervical dilatation < 5cm and good uterine contractions should be observed for 2 hours and admitted to labor ward if the cervix dilates 1 cm or more. (Conditional)

normal-labor-9.sourceText: Criteria for admission to labor ward
normal-labor-9.displayText: Criteria for admission to labor ward in low-risk women: active stage of labor and rupture of membranes. (Conditional)

normal-labor-10.sourceText: Maintain the minimum level of birth intervention compatible with safety.
normal-labor-10.displayText: Maintain the minimum level of birth intervention compatible with safety. (Strong)

normal-labor-11.displayText: Explain to the woman that they should drink during labor when they are thirsty, and that isotonic drinks may be more beneficial than water. (Strong)

normal-labor-12.sourceText: We recommend against routine perineal/pubic shaving prior to giving vaginal birth.
normal-labor-12.displayText: We recommend against routine perineal/pubic shaving prior to giving vaginal birth. (Conditional)

normal-labor-13.sourceText: We recommend against administration of an enema for reducing the use of labor augmentation.
normal-labor-13.displayText: We recommend against administration of an enema for reducing the use of labor augmentation. (Strong)

normal-labor-14.sourceText: Labor may not naturally accelerate until a cervical dilatation threshold of 5 cm is reached. Therefore, the use of medical interventions to accelerate labor and birth (such as oxytocin augmentation or caesarean section) before this threshold is not recommended, provided fetal and maternal conditions are reassuring
normal-labor-14.displayText: Labor may not naturally accelerate until a cervical dilatation threshold of 5 cm is reached. Therefore, the use of medical interventions to accelerate labor and birth (such as oxytocin augmentation or caesarean section) before this threshold is not recommended. (Strong)

normal-labor-15.sourceText: Duration of the active first stage: The duration of active first stage (from 5 cm until full cervical dilatation) usually does not extend beyond 12 hours in first labors, and usually does not extend beyond 10 hours in subsequent labors.
normal-labor-15.displayText: The duration of active first stage (from 5 cm until full cervical dilatation) usually does not extend beyond 12 hours in first labors and usually does not extend beyond 10 hours in subsequent labors. (GPS)

normal-labor-16.sourceText: Progress of the first stage of labor: In active labor, cervical dilatation of 0.5 cm per hour (2 cm in 4 hours) is considered normal
normal-labor-16.displayText: In active labor, cervical dilatation of 0.5 cm per hour (2 cm in 4 hours) is considered normal. (Strong)

normal-labor-17.sourceText: We recommend against the use of active management of labor for prevention of delay in labor.
normal-labor-17.displayText: We recommend against the use of active management of labor for prevention of delay in labor. (Conditional)

normal-labor-18.sourceText: Do not routinely use amniotomy and or oxytocin to prevent delayed progress in 1st stage of labor.
normal-labor-18.displayText: Do not routinely use amniotomy and/or oxytocin to prevent delayed progress in 1st stage of labor. (Conditional)

normal-labor-19.sourceText: We recommend against the use of oxytocin for prevention of delay in labor in women receiving epidural analgesia.
normal-labor-19.displayText: We recommend against the use of oxytocin for prevention of delay in labor in women receiving epidural analgesia. (Strong)

normal-labor-20.displayText: Minimize vaginal examination: VE at intervals of two hours is recommended for routine assessment of active first stage of labor in low-risk women. (GPS)

normal-labor-21.sourceText: Avoid supine position as it is associated with adverse effects including
normal-labor-21.displayText: Avoid supine position as it is associated with adverse effects including supine hypotension and abnormal FHR. (Strong)

normal-labor-22.sourceText: We recommend against the use of continuous cardiotocography for assessment of fetal well-being in normal labor
normal-labor-22.displayText: We recommend against the use of continuous cardiotocography for assessment of fetal well-being in normal labor. (Strong)

normal-labor-23.displayText: Intermittent auscultation of the fetal heart rate with either a Doppler ultrasound device or a Pinard fetal stethoscope is recommended for normal labor. Auscultate every 15-30 minutes in active first stage and every 5 minutes in the second stage, each for at least 1 minute. (Strong)

normal-labor-24.sourceText: Start using partogram when active labor is confirmed for documentation and providing a visual overview of progress.
normal-labor-24.displayText: Start using partogram when active labor is confirmed for documentation and providing a visual overview of progress. (Strong)

normal-labor-25.sourceText: fresh red bleeding or blood-stained liquor
normal-labor-25.displayText: If any warning signs are present or developed during labor, consult a specialist care: pulse over 120 beats/minute, BP of 160/110 mmHg or more, temperature of 38°C or above, fresh red bleeding or blood-stained liquor, the new appearance of meconium, or confirmed delay in the first stage of labor. (Strong)

normal-labor-26.sourceText: If delayed progress in the established first stage is suspected, assess:
normal-labor-26.displayText: If delayed progress in the established first stage is suspected, assess: cervical dilatation of less than 2 cm in 4 hours, descent and rotation of the baby's head, strength, duration and frequency of uterine contraction. (Strong)

normal-labor-27.sourceText: For women with intact membranes in whom delay in the established first stage of labor is confirmed:
normal-labor-27.displayText: For women with intact membranes in whom delay in the established first stage of labor is confirmed, consider amniotomy if membranes are intact, oxytocin if inertia was diagnosed, and repeat vaginal examination 2 hours later. (GPS)

normal-labor-28.displayText: If oxytocin is used in the first stage of labor, ensure that the time between increments of the dose is no more frequent than every 30 minutes and increase oxytocin until there are 3 to 4 contractions in 10 minutes. (Strong)

normal-labor-29.sourceText: Oxytocin must be discontinued immediately if there is abnormality in fetal heart rate is observed.
normal-labor-29.displayText: Oxytocin must be discontinued immediately if there is abnormality in fetal heart rate. (Strong)

normal-labor-30.sourceText: Application of manual fundal pressure to facilitate childbirth during the second stage of labor is not recommended .
normal-labor-30.displayText: Application of manual fundal pressure to facilitate childbirth during the second stage of labor is not recommended. (Strong)

normal-labor-31.sourceText: For women in the second stage of labor, techniques to reduce perineal trauma and facilitate spontaneous birth (including perineal massage, warm compresses and a hands on guarding of the perineum) are recommended
normal-labor-31.displayText: For women in the second stage of labor, techniques to reduce perineal trauma and facilitate spontaneous birth (including perineal massage, warm compresses and a hands on guarding of the perineum) are recommended. (Strong)

normal-labor-32.sourceText: Routine or liberal use of episiotomy is not recommended for women undergoing spontaneous vaginal birth.
normal-labor-32.displayText: Routine or liberal use of episiotomy is not recommended for women undergoing spontaneous vaginal birth. (Strong)

normal-labor-33.sourceText: If an episiotomy is performed, the recommended technique is a mediolateral episiotomy originating at the vaginal fourchette and usually directed to the right side. The angle to the vertical axis should be between 45 and 60 degrees at the time of the episiotomy.
normal-labor-33.displayText: If an episiotomy is performed, the recommended technique is a mediolateral episiotomy originating at the vaginal fourchette and usually directed to the right side. The angle to the vertical axis should be between 45 and 60 degrees. (Strong)

normal-labor-34.sourceText: Delay in active second stage is diagnosed when:
normal-labor-34.displayText: Delay in active second stage is diagnosed when: In nulliparous woman, insufficient flexion/rotation/descent within 1 hour or second stage duration > 2 hours. In multiparous woman, insufficient flexion/rotation/descent within 30 minutes or second stage duration > 1 hour. (GPS)

normal-labor-35.displayText: Operative vaginal delivery in second stage of labor by experienced and well-trained physicians should be considered a safe, acceptable alternative to cesarean delivery. (Strong)

normal-labor-36.sourceText: The use of uterotonics for prevention of PPH during the third stage of labor is recommended for all births.
normal-labor-36.displayText: The use of uterotonics for prevention of PPH during the third stage of labor is recommended for all births. (Strong)

normal-labor-37.sourceText: Late cord clamping (performed approximately 1 to 3 minutes after birth) is recommended for all births while initiating simultaneous essential newborn care.
normal-labor-37.displayText: Late cord clamping (performed approximately 1 to 3 minutes after birth) is recommended for all births while initiating simultaneous essential newborn care. (Strong)

normal-labor-38.displayText: Consider Controlled cord traction (CCT) as part of active/modified active management of third stage. (Strong)

normal-labor-39.sourceText: In most circumstances, oxytocin is the prophylactic uterotonic of choice.
normal-labor-39.displayText: In most circumstances, oxytocin is the prophylactic uterotonic of choice. For vaginal birth with IV access: Oxytocin 10 IU IV injected slowly over 3-5 minutes. For CS birth: Oxytocin 5 IU IV over 1-2 minutes. (Strong)

normal-labor-40.displayText: Diagnose a prolonged third stage of labor if it is not completed within 30 minutes of the birth with active management or within 60 minutes with physiological management. (Strong)

normal-labor-41.sourceText: Perform a thorough examination of the placenta and membranes:
normal-labor-41.displayText: Perform a thorough examination of the placenta and membranes including general shape and appearance, calcification or infarctions, evidence of abruption, missing cotyledons, and succenturiate lobes. (Strong)

normal-labor-42.sourceText: Postpartum abdominal uterine tonus assessment for early identification of uterine atony is recommended for all women.
normal-labor-42.displayText: Postpartum abdominal uterine tonus assessment for early identification of uterine atony is recommended for all women. (Strong)

normal-labor-43.sourceText: After an uncomplicated vaginal birth in a health care facility, we advise that healthy mothers and newborns receive care in the facility for 12 - 24 hours after birth.
normal-labor-43.displayText: After an uncomplicated vaginal birth in a health care facility, we advise that healthy mothers and newborns receive care in the facility for 12 - 24 hours after birth. (GPS)

normal-labor-44.sourceText: Advise women that breathing exercises, and having a shower or bath, may reduce pain during the latent first stage of labor.
normal-labor-44.displayText: Advise women that breathing exercises and having a shower or bath may reduce pain during the latent first stage of labor. (Conditional)

normal-labor-45.sourceText: - Parenteral opioids, such as fentanyl, diamorphine and pethidine, are options for healthy pregnant women requesting pain relief during labor, depending on a woman s preferences and availability.
normal-labor-45.displayText: Parenteral opioids, such as fentanyl, diamorphine and pethidine, are options for healthy pregnant women requesting pain relief during labor, depending on a woman's preferences and availability. (Conditional)

normal-labor-46.sourceText: Epidural analgesia may be offered for healthy pregnant women requesting pain relief during labor, depending on a woman s preferences and availability.
normal-labor-46.displayText: Epidural analgesia may be offered for healthy pregnant women requesting pain relief during labor, depending on a woman's preferences and availability. (Conditional)

normal-labor-47.sourceText: - Do not routinely use oxytocin in the second stage of labor for women with epidural analgesia.
normal-labor-47.displayText: Do not routinely use oxytocin in the second stage of labor for women with epidural analgesia. (Strong)

normal-labor-48.displayText: Operative vaginal delivery with forceps or vacuum in second stage of labor by experienced and well-trained physicians should be considered safe, acceptable alternative to cesarean delivery. (Strong)

normal-labor-49.sourceText: If there is a positive fluid balance of 1500 ml or more, or there are clinical concerns (for example, signs and symptoms of hyponatremia):
normal-labor-49.displayText: If there is a positive fluid balance of 1500 ml or more, or there are clinical concerns (for example, signs and symptoms of hyponatremia): explain the concerns and avoid excessive intravenous fluids. (Strong)

normal-labor-50.sourceText: Undertake perineal repair using a continuous non-locked suturing technique for the vaginal wall and muscle layer.
normal-labor-50.displayText: Undertake perineal repair using a continuous non-locked suturing technique for the vaginal wall and muscle layer and continuous subcuticular for the skin. (Strong)

normal-labor-51.sourceText: In Rh negative mothers with Rh positive husband, request indirect Coomb s test if available
normal-labor-51.displayText: In Rh negative mothers with Rh positive husband, request indirect Coomb s test if available and administer anti-D immunoglobulin. (Strong)

normal-labor-52.sourceText: If spontaneous rupture of membranes (SROM) suspected, consider a dry sterile speculum examination.
normal-labor-52.displayText: If spontaneous rupture of membranes (SROM) suspected, consider a dry sterile speculum examination and assess amniotic fluid. (Strong)

normal-labor-53.displayText: Operative vaginal delivery with vacuum or forceps in second stage of labor by experienced and well-trained physicians should be considered safe, acceptable alternative to cesarean delivery. (Strong)

preterm-labor-0.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-0.sourceText: 1.1. Assess risk factors preconception and early pregnancy with a comprehensive review of all previous pregnancies because the most important historical risk factor is prior spontaneous PTL.
preterm-labor-0.displayText: Assess risk factors preconception and early pregnancy with a comprehensive review of all previous pregnancies because the most important historical risk factor is prior spontaneous PTL. (Strong)

preterm-labor-1.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-1.sourceText: 2.4.1 Recommend routine cervical length measurement to women during the mid-trimester morphology (18 20 weeks) ultrasound scan with the cervical length documented in medical records 25-27
preterm-labor-1.displayText: Recommend routine cervical length measurement to women during the mid-trimester morphology (18–20 weeks) ultrasound scan with the cervical length documented. (GPS)

preterm-labor-2.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-2.sourceText: For singleton pregnancies recommend vaginal progesterone 200 mg by night from 16–36 weeks gestation for women with a history of spontaneous preterm birth or short cervical length ≤ 25 mm. (Strong)
preterm-labor-2.displayText: For singleton pregnancies recommend vaginal progesterone 200 mg by night from 16–36 weeks gestation for women with a history of spontaneous preterm birth or short cervical length ≤ 25 mm. (Strong)

preterm-labor-3.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-3.sourceText: Cervical cerclage may be indicated (individualize decisions) for women with history of spontaneous preterm birth and ultrasound-indicated cervical length ≤ 25 mm before 24 weeks. (Conditional)
preterm-labor-3.displayText: Cervical cerclage may be indicated (individualize decisions) for women with history of spontaneous preterm birth and ultrasound-indicated cervical length ≤ 25 mm before 24 weeks. (Conditional)

preterm-labor-4.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-4.sourceText: 5.2 If the clinical assessment suggests that the woman is in suspected preterm labor and she is 29 6 weeks pregnant or less, advise treatment as diagnosed preterm labor as described in the sections on tocolysis and maternal corticosteroids.
preterm-labor-4.displayText: If the clinical assessment suggests that the woman is in suspected preterm labor and she is 29+6 weeks pregnant or less, advise treatment as diagnosed preterm labor. (Strong)

preterm-labor-5.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-5.sourceText: Tocolysis is recommended to give time for a course of corticosteroid therapy or to allow in-utero transfer to an obstetric center with higher-level neonatal care.
preterm-labor-5.displayText: Tocolysis is recommended to give time for a course of corticosteroid therapy or to allow in-utero transfer to an obstetric center with higher-level neonatal care. (Strong)

preterm-labor-6.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-6.sourceText: Antenatal corticosteroids should be offered to women between 24+0 and 33+6 weeks of gestation who are at high risk of imminent preterm delivery within 7 days. (Strong)
preterm-labor-6.displayText: Antenatal corticosteroids should be offered to women between 24+0 and 33+6 weeks of gestation who are at high risk of imminent preterm delivery within 7 days. (Strong)

preterm-labor-7.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-7.sourceText: Magnesium sulfate should be offered for fetal neuroprotection to women between 24+0 and 31+6 weeks of gestation in established preterm labor or having a planned preterm birth. (Strong)
preterm-labor-7.displayText: Magnesium sulfate should be offered for fetal neuroprotection to women between 24+0 and 31+6 weeks of gestation in established preterm labor or having a planned preterm birth. (Strong)

preterm-labor-8.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-8.sourceText: Maintenance tocolytic therapy is not recommended for women who have had an episode of threatened preterm labor that responded to initial treatment. (Conditional)
preterm-labor-8.displayText: Maintenance tocolytic therapy is not recommended for women who have had an episode of threatened preterm labor that responded to initial treatment. (Conditional)

preterm-labor-9.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-9.sourceText: Antibiotics are not recommended for women in spontaneous preterm labor with intact membranes and no evidence of infection. (Strong)
preterm-labor-9.displayText: Antibiotics are not recommended for women in spontaneous preterm labor with intact membranes and no evidence of infection. (Strong)

preterm-labor-10.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-10.sourceText: Offer women with PPROM oral erythromycin 250 mg 4 times a day for a maximum of 10 days or until the woman is in established labour (whichever is sooner). (Strong)
preterm-labor-10.displayText: Offer women with PPROM oral erythromycin 250 mg 4 times a day for a maximum of 10 days or until the woman is in established labour (whichever is sooner). (Strong)

preterm-labor-11.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-11.sourceText: Fetal Fibronectin testing: quantitative fetal fibronectin provides high negative predictive value in the assessment and management of suspected preterm labor. (Conditional)
preterm-labor-11.displayText: Fetal Fibronectin testing: quantitative fetal fibronectin provides high negative predictive value in the assessment and management of suspected preterm labor. (Conditional)

preterm-labor-12.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-12.sourceText: Preterm birth remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality globally and within Egypt; clinical interventions reduce respiratory distress and adverse outcomes. (Strong)
preterm-labor-12.displayText: Preterm birth remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality globally and within Egypt; clinical interventions reduce respiratory distress and adverse outcomes. (Strong)

preterm-labor-13.bookTitle: Prevention And Management Of Preterm Labor
preterm-labor-13.sourceText: Suspected PTL (symptoms present but labor not established)
preterm-labor-13.displayText: Offer admission for reassessment and therapeutic interventions for women with suspected PTL and diagnosed PPROM; offer oral erythromycin 250 mg 4 times a day for up to 10 days. (Strong)
